explanation: Combined one-day work = 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6, so together they take 6 days.

text: A completes a job in 12 days and B completes the same job in 24 days. Working together they will complete it in:
explanation: Combined one-day work = 1/12 + 1/24 = 3/24 = 1/8, so they take 8 days.

text: If 15 men can complete a work in 20 days, then 25 men will complete it in:
explanation: Total work = 15 x 20 = 300 man-days, so 25 men need 300/25 = 12 days.

text: A can do a work in 20 days. He works for 5 days and leaves, and B, who alone can do the whole work in 30 days, finishes the remainder in:
explanation: A completes 5/20 = 1/4 of the work, so B must do 3/4 of it, taking 3/4 x 30 = 22.5 days.

text: A and B together finish a work in 12 days while A alone finishes it in 20 days. B alone will take:
explanation: B's one-day work = 1/12 - 1/20 = 5/60 - 3/60 = 2/60 = 1/30, so B alone takes 30 days.

text: One pipe fills a tank in 6 hours and another fills it in 12 hours. Opened together they will fill it in:
explanation: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the tank per hour, so 4 hours are needed.

text: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours while pipe B empties the full tank in 15 hours. With both pipes open the tank fills in:
explanation: Net filling rate = 1/10 - 1/15 = 3/30 - 2/30 = 1/30 per hour, so the tank fills in 30 hours.

text: A is twice as good a workman as B and together they finish a work in 12 days. B alone will finish it in:
explanation: Their rates are in the ratio 2 : 1, so B does one-third of the joint work and needs 3 x 12 = 36 days.

text: A, B and C can do a work in 10, 12 and 15 days respectively. Working together they will finish it in:
Twelve men working 6 hours a day complete a job in 10 days. Fifteen men working 8 hours a day will complete the same job in:
explanation: Total work = 12 x 6 x 10 = 720 man-hours, so the time = 720/(15 x 8) = 6 days.

text: A and B together complete a work in 8 days, while A, B and C together complete it in 6 days. C alone will complete it in:
explanation: C's one-day work = 1/6 - 1/8 = 4/24 - 3/24 = 1/24, so C alone takes 24 days.

text: If 5 machines produce 500 units in 10 hours, the number of units 8 identical machines will produce in the same 10 hours is:
explanation: Each machine makes 100 units in 10 hours, so 8 machines make 8 x 100 = 800 units.

text: A car covers 240 km in 4 hours. Its average speed is:
explanation: Speed = distance/time = 240/4 = 60 km/h.

text: A speed of 72 km/h expressed in metres per second is:
explanation: Multiply by 5/18: 72 x 5/18 = 20 m/s.

text: A speed of 15 metres per second expressed in kilometres per hour is:
explanation: Multiply by 18/5: 15 x 18/5 = 54 km/h.

text: A train 150 metres long crosses a pole in 10 seconds. Its speed is:
A train 200 metres long running at 36 km/h crosses a platform 100 metres long in:
explanation: The train covers 200 + 100 = 300 m at 36 km/h = 10 m/s, needing 300/10 = 30 seconds.

text: The distance covered in 2 hours and 20 minutes at a speed of 45 km/h is:
explanation: 2 hours 20 minutes = 7/3 hours, so the distance = 45 x 7/3 = 105 km.

text: The time taken to cover 360 km at a uniform speed of 80 km/h is:
explanation: Time = 360/80 = 4.5 hours.

text: A man travels from A to B at 60 km/h and returns at 40 km/h. His average speed for the whole journey is:
explanation: Average speed = 2ab/(a+b) = 2 x 60 x 40/100 = 48 km/h.

text: Two trains 150 metres and 100 metres long run in opposite directions at 60 km/h and 40 km/h. The time they take to cross each other is:
explanation: Relative speed = 100 km/h = 250/9 m/s and the combined length is 250 m, so the time = 250 x 9/250 = 9 seconds.

text: A man covers a distance in 3 hours walking at 5 km/h. To cover the same distance in 2 hours and 30 minutes he must walk at:
explanation: The distance is 15 km, so the required speed = 15/2.5 = 6 km/h.

text: A boat whose speed in still water is 10 km/h travels 36 km downstream in a stream flowing at 2 km/h. The time taken is:
explanation: Downstream speed = 10 + 2 = 12 km/h, so the time = 36/12 = 3 hours.

text: A train running at 54 km/h crosses a bridge 300 metres long in 30 seconds. The length of the train is:
explanation: At 15 m/s the train covers 450 m in 30 seconds, so its length = 450 - 300 = 150 m.

text: Two cars start together from the same point in the same direction at 50 km/h and 40 km/h. After 3 hours the distance between them is:
explanation: They separate at 10 km/h, so after 3 hours the gap is 30 km.

text: A cyclist covers 20 km in 50 minutes. His speed is:
explanation: 50 minutes = 5/6 hour, so the speed = 20 x 6/5 = 24 km/h.

text: A invests Rs 5,000 and B invests Rs 7,000 in a business for the same period. Out of a profit of Rs 6,000, B's share is:
explanation: Profits are shared in the ratio 5 : 7, so B receives 6,000 x 7/12 = Rs 3,500.

text: A and B invest Rs 8,000 and Rs 12,000 respectively for the same period. Out of a total profit of Rs 5,000, A receives:
explanation: The capital ratio is 2 : 3, so A receives 5,000 x 2/5 = Rs 2,000.

text: A invests Rs 3,000 for 12 months and B invests Rs 4,000 for 6 months. Out of a profit of Rs 10,000, A's share is:
explanation: Capital-months are 36,000 and 24,000, a ratio of 3 : 2, so A gets 10,000 x 3/5 = Rs 6,000.

text: Three partners invest Rs 4,000, Rs 6,000 and Rs 10,000 for the same period. Out of a profit of Rs 10,000 the third partner receives:
explanation: The ratio is 2 : 3 : 5, so the third partner receives 10,000 x 5/10 = Rs 5,000.

text: A and B share profits in the ratio 3 : 5. If B's share exceeds A's by Rs 800, the total profit is:
explanation: The difference is 2 parts = Rs 800, so one part = Rs 400 and the total of 8 parts = Rs 3,200.

text: Two partners invest capitals in the ratio 2 : 3 for periods in the ratio 3 : 2. Their profits will be shared in the ratio:
explanation: Profit shares follow capital x time = 6 : 6, which reduces to 1 : 1.

text: A 40-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. The quantity of milk in it is:
explanation: Milk = 40 x 3/4 = 30 litres.

text: A 60-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1. The water that must be added to make the ratio 1 : 1 is:
explanation: The mixture has 40 litres of milk and 20 litres of water, so 20 more litres of water make both equal.

text: Rice costing Rs 40 per kg is mixed with rice costing Rs 60 per kg in the ratio 3 : 2. The cost of the mixture per kg is:
In what ratio must tea costing Rs 60 per kg be mixed with tea costing Rs 100 per kg so that the mixture costs Rs 75 per kg?
explanation: By alligation the ratio is (100 - 75) : (75 - 60) = 25 : 15 = 5 : 3.

text: Twenty litres of a milk solution contains 10% water. The quantity of water in it is:
explanation: Water = 10% of 20 = 2 litres.

text: Fifty litres of a mixture contains 20% alcohol. After adding 10 litres of water the percentage of alcohol becomes:
explanation: The alcohol stays at 10 litres while the total becomes 60 litres, so the strength is 10/60 x 100 = 16.67%.

text: The LCM of 12 and 18 is:
The HCF of 24 and 36 is:
explanation: The common factors give 2^2 x 3 = 12, the greatest common divisor.

text: The LCM of 8, 12 and 20 is:
explanation: Taking the highest powers 2^3, 3 and 5 gives 8 x 3 x 5 = 120.

text: The HCF of 36, 60 and 84 is:
explanation: Each number is divisible by 2^2 x 3 = 12 and by no larger common factor.

text: The product of two numbers is 216 and their HCF is 6. Their LCM is:
explanation: LCM = product/HCF = 216/6 = 36.

text: The smallest number exactly divisible by 6, 8 and 12 is:
explanation: The required number is the LCM of 6, 8 and 12, which is 24.

text: The least number which when divided by 5, 6 and 8 leaves a remainder of 3 in each case is:
explanation: The LCM of 5, 6 and 8 is 120, so the number is 120 + 3 = 123.

text: The LCM of two numbers is 48 and their HCF is 8. If one number is 16, the other number is:
explanation: The product of the numbers equals LCM x HCF = 384, so the other number = 384/16 = 24.

text: The greatest four-digit number exactly divisible by 15, 25 and 40 is:
explanation: The LCM of 15, 25 and 40 is 600, and 600 x 16 = 9,600 is the largest such four-digit multiple.

text: The value of 3/4 + 2/5 is:
The greatest of the fractions 2/3, 3/5, 5/8 and 7/12 is:
explanation: As decimals they are 0.667, 0.600, 0.625 and 0.583, so 2/3 is the largest.

text: The product 0.6 x 0.05 is:
explanation: 6 x 5 = 30 and the factors carry three decimal places in total, giving 0.030 = 0.03.

text: Expressed as a decimal, 7/8 equals:
explanation: Dividing 7 by 8 gives 0.875.

text: One-half of two-thirds of three-fourths of 240 is:
explanation: The three fractions multiply to 1/4, and 240/4 = 60.

text: The value of 2.5 divided by 0.05 is:
The value of 5/6 - 3/8 is:
explanation: Using 24 as the common denominator, 20/24 - 9/24 = 11/24.

text: Expressed as a fraction in its lowest terms, 0.125 equals:
explanation: 0.125 = 125/1000, which reduces to 1/8.

text: The organelle known as the powerhouse of the cell is the
explanation: Aerobic respiration is completed in the mitochondrion, which releases most of the cell's energy in the form of ATP.

text: Protein synthesis in a cell takes place on the
explanation: Ribosomes translate messenger RNA into polypeptide chains, so they are the site of protein synthesis.

text: The cell organelles called suicide bags because of their digestive enzymes are the
explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that can digest the cell's own contents if the organelle bursts.

text: The cell wall of a plant cell is mainly composed of
explanation: Plant cell walls are chiefly cellulose; chitin occurs in fungal walls and peptidoglycan in bacterial walls.

text: The cell was first observed and named by
explanation: Robert Hooke in 1665 examined a thin slice of cork under his microscope and called the compartments he saw cells.

text: The nucleus of the cell was discovered by
explanation: Robert Brown described the nucleus in plant cells in 1831.

text: The main function of the Golgi apparatus is
options: Packaging and secretion of cell products
explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, packages and dispatches materials made in the endoplasmic reticulum.

text: The largest organ of the human body is the
explanation: The skin covers the entire body surface and is the largest organ by both weight and area.

text: The largest gland in the human body is the
explanation: The liver is the largest gland; it secretes bile and performs numerous metabolic functions.

text: The number of bones in the normal adult human skeleton is
explanation: An adult skeleton has 206 bones; a newborn has about 270, many of which fuse during growth.

text: The longest bone in the human body is the
explanation: The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest and strongest bone of the human body.

text: The smallest bone in the human body is the
explanation: The stapes, or stirrup bone, of the middle ear is the smallest bone in the body.

text: The structural and functional unit of the kidney is the
explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons, which filter blood and form urine.

text: The structural and functional unit of the nervous system is the
explanation: The neuron, or nerve cell, transmits impulses; the axon is only a part of a neuron.

text: The gland known as the master gland of the human body is the
explanation: The pituitary secretes hormones that control the activity of most other endocrine glands.

text: The largest artery of the human body is the
explanation: The aorta leaves the left ventricle and distributes oxygenated blood to the whole body.

text: Bile secreted by the liver is stored in the
explanation: Bile made in the liver is concentrated and stored in the gall bladder before release into the duodenum.

text: The voice box of the human respiratory tract is the
explanation: The larynx houses the vocal cords, whose vibration produces sound.

text: The number of teeth in a normal adult human being is
explanation: A complete adult set has 32 permanent teeth, compared with 20 milk teeth in a child.

text: The sheet of muscle separating the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity is the
explanation: The diaphragm separates the chest from the abdomen and contracts during inhalation to enlarge the chest cavity.

text: Urea is chiefly formed in the
explanation: The liver converts ammonia from protein breakdown into urea, which the kidneys then excrete.

text: The blood group known as the universal donor is
explanation: Group O red cells carry neither A nor B antigen, so they are not attacked by the recipient's anti-A or anti-B antibodies.

text: The blood group known as the universal recipient is
explanation: Group AB plasma contains neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies, so blood of any ABO group can be received.

text: The ABO system of human blood groups was discovered by
explanation: Karl Landsteiner identified the ABO blood groups in 1901 and received the Nobel Prize for the work.

text: The Rh factor of human blood takes its name from the
explanation: The antigen was first detected in the blood of the rhesus monkey, hence the name Rh factor.

text: In an adult human being, red blood cells are produced mainly in the
explanation: Red bone marrow is the site of erythrocyte formation after birth; the liver performs this role only in the foetus.

text: The average life span of a human red blood cell is about
explanation: Erythrocytes survive roughly 120 days before being destroyed, mainly in the spleen.

text: The metal present in haemoglobin is
explanation: Each haem group of haemoglobin contains an iron atom that binds oxygen reversibly.

text: Clotting of blood is brought about mainly by
explanation: Platelets, or thrombocytes, collect at a wound and set off the reactions that form a fibrin clot.

text: The straw-coloured fluid in which blood cells remain suspended is called
explanation: Plasma is the fluid part of whole blood; serum is plasma from which clotting proteins have been removed.

text: A mature human red blood cell lacks a
explanation: Mature erythrocytes lose their nucleus, which leaves more room for haemoglobin.

text: The natural pacemaker of the human heart is the
explanation: The sinoatrial node in the right atrium generates the impulse that sets the heart rate.

text: The circulation of blood in the human body was first described by
explanation: William Harvey demonstrated in 1628 that blood circulates in a closed circuit driven by the heart.

text: Oxygenated blood is carried from the lungs to the heart by the
explanation: The pulmonary vein is the only vein carrying oxygenated blood, returning it from the lungs to the left atrium.

text: The normal blood pressure of a healthy adult is taken as
explanation: A systolic pressure of about 120 mm Hg and a diastolic pressure of about 80 mm Hg is regarded as normal.

text: The valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle is the
explanation: The bicuspid or mitral valve guards the left atrioventricular opening; the tricuspid valve lies on the right side.

text: The pH of normal human blood is approximately
explanation: Blood is slightly alkaline and is buffered at a pH of about 7.35 to 7.45.

text: Deficiency of vitamin C in the diet causes
explanation: Lack of ascorbic acid weakens connective tissue, producing scurvy with bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

text: Deficiency of vitamin D in children causes
explanation: Vitamin D is needed for calcium absorption; without it bones soften and deform, a condition called rickets.

text: Night blindness results from the deficiency of
explanation: Vitamin A is required to make rhodopsin, the pigment of the rod cells that gives vision in dim light.

text: Beriberi is caused by the deficiency of
explanation: Beriberi results from a lack of thiamine, vitamin B1, and affects the nerves and heart.

text: Pellagra is caused by the deficiency of
explanation: Pellagra follows a shortage of niacin, vitamin B3, and shows as dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia.

text: Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of
explanation: Vitamin B12 is needed for the maturation of red blood cells; its lack produces pernicious anaemia.

text: The vitamin essential for the normal clotting of blood is
explanation: Vitamin K is required by the liver to make prothrombin and other clotting factors.

text: The chemical name of vitamin C is
explanation: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid; retinol is vitamin A and calciferol is vitamin D.

text: Which of the following vitamins is water soluble?
explanation: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble, while vitamin C and the B group dissolve in water.

text: The metal present in vitamin B12 is
explanation: Vitamin B12, cyanocobalamin, contains a cobalt atom at the centre of its corrin ring.

text: Goitre is caused by the deficiency of
explanation: Iodine is needed to make thyroxine; without it the thyroid enlarges, producing goitre.

text: The chemical name of vitamin E is
explanation: Vitamin E is tocopherol, an antioxidant that protects cell membranes.

text: Insulin is secreted by the
explanation: The beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin.

text: Diabetes mellitus is caused by the deficiency of
explanation: Insufficient insulin prevents cells from taking up glucose, so blood sugar rises and sugar appears in the urine.

text: The pancreatic hormone that raises the level of glucose in the blood is
explanation: Glucagon from the alpha cells of the pancreas converts stored glycogen into glucose, raising blood sugar.

text: The hormone released in large amounts during fear or anger is
explanation: Adrenaline from the adrenal medulla prepares the body for fight or flight by raising heart rate and blood sugar.

text: Excessive secretion of growth hormone during childhood results in
explanation: Oversecretion of growth hormone before the growing ends of bones close causes abnormal height, called gigantism.

text: Deficiency of thyroxine in infancy leads to
explanation: Lack of thyroxine in infancy stunts physical growth and mental development, a condition called cretinism.

text: The level of calcium in the blood is regulated by
explanation: Parathormone from the parathyroid glands raises blood calcium by mobilising it from bone.

text: The principal male sex hormone is
explanation: Testosterone is secreted by the testes and controls male secondary sexual characters.

text: The digestion of starch begins in the
explanation: Salivary amylase in the mouth starts breaking starch down into maltose.

text: The digestion of protein begins in the
explanation: Pepsin, activated by hydrochloric acid in the stomach, begins the breakdown of proteins into peptides.

text: The acid present in human gastric juice is
explanation: Hydrochloric acid makes the stomach contents acidic, activates pepsin and kills many swallowed microbes.

text: Most of the absorption of digested food takes place in the
explanation: The villi lining the small intestine give a huge surface for absorbing digested nutrients.

text: The chief function of the large intestine is the absorption of
explanation: The large intestine reabsorbs most of the water from the undigested residue before faeces are formed.

text: Bile assists in the digestion of
explanation: Bile salts emulsify fats into tiny droplets so that lipase can act on them more easily.

text: The vermiform appendix in man is attached to the
explanation: The appendix is a narrow vestigial tube projecting from the caecum at the start of the large intestine.

text: Exchange of gases in the lungs takes place in the
explanation: The thin, moist walls of the alveoli are surrounded by capillaries, allowing oxygen and carbon dioxide to diffuse.

text: The energy currency of the living cell is
explanation: Adenosine triphosphate stores energy in its phosphate bonds and releases it wherever the cell needs it.

text: During strenuous exercise, muscle cells respiring anaerobically produce
explanation: When oxygen supply falls short, glucose is converted to lactic acid, which causes muscle fatigue and cramp.

text: Carbon monoxide is poisonous to human beings because it
options: Combines with haemoglobin more readily than oxygen
explanation: Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin far more strongly than oxygen does, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and starving tissues of oxygen.

text: The flap of cartilage that prevents food from entering the windpipe during swallowing is the
explanation: The epiglottis folds over the opening of the larynx while food is being swallowed.

text: Malaria in human beings is caused by a
explanation: Malaria is caused by the protozoan parasite Plasmodium, which multiplies in the liver and red blood cells.

text: Malaria is transmitted to man by the
explanation: Only the female Anopheles takes blood meals and thus transfers Plasmodium from person to person.

text: Dengue fever is transmitted by the
explanation: The Aedes aegypti mosquito, which bites mostly by day, carries the dengue virus.

text: The causative organism of tuberculosis is
explanation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, identified by Robert Koch, causes tuberculosis and spreads through droplets.

text: AIDS is caused by
explanation: The human immunodeficiency virus destroys helper T cells and so cripples immunity.

text: Cholera is caused by
explanation: The bacterium Vibrio cholerae spreads through contaminated water and causes severe watery diarrhoea.

text: Typhoid fever is caused by
explanation: Salmonella typhi, taken in with contaminated food or water, causes typhoid fever.

text: Rabies is usually transmitted to man through the
explanation: The rabies virus is present in the saliva of infected animals and enters through a bite wound.

text: Sleeping sickness is transmitted by the
explanation: The tsetse fly of tropical Africa carries the protozoan Trypanosoma that causes sleeping sickness.

text: Bubonic plague is transmitted to man mainly by the
explanation: The rat flea carries the plague bacterium Yersinia pestis from infected rodents to human beings.

text: Kala azar, or visceral leishmaniasis, is transmitted by the
explanation: The bite of an infected sand fly transfers the protozoan Leishmania to human beings.

text: Hepatitis is a disease affecting the
explanation: Hepatitis means inflammation of the liver and is most often caused by viruses A, B, C, D or E.

text: Antibiotics such as penicillin are effective against bacteria but not against
explanation: Viruses have no cell wall or metabolic machinery of their own, so antibacterial antibiotics do not affect them.

text: Penicillin was discovered by
explanation: Alexander Fleming noticed in 1928 that the mould Penicillium notatum killed bacteria on his culture plate.

text: The first vaccine, used against smallpox, was developed by
explanation: Edward Jenner showed in 1796 that inoculation with cowpox material protected against smallpox.

text: The BCG vaccine gives protection against
explanation: Bacillus Calmette Guerin vaccine is given in infancy to protect against tuberculosis.

text: Oral rehydration salts are given chiefly in the treatment of
explanation: ORS replaces the water and salts lost in diarrhoea and so prevents dehydration.

text: Vaccination protects a person by producing
explanation: A vaccine makes the body produce its own antibodies and memory cells, which is active immunity.

text: The number of chromosomes in a normal human body cell is
explanation: Human somatic cells carry 46 chromosomes, that is 23 pairs, of which one pair determines sex.

text: The sex chromosomes of a normal human male are
explanation: Males carry one X and one Y chromosome, while females carry two X chromosomes.

text: The sex of a human child is determined by the
explanation: The ovum always carries an X chromosome, so the sex depends on whether the sperm carries X or Y.

text: The father of genetics is
explanation: Gregor Mendel worked out the laws of inheritance and is regarded as the father of genetics.

text: The double helix model of DNA was proposed by
explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick described the double helical structure of DNA in 1953.

text: The nitrogenous base present in RNA but not in DNA is
explanation: RNA carries uracil in place of the thymine found in DNA.

text: Down syndrome results from an extra copy of chromosome number
explanation: Down syndrome, or trisomy 21, occurs when three copies of chromosome 21 are present instead of two.

text: Haemophilia is an inherited disorder in which
options: Red cells are produced in excess
explanation: Haemophilia is a sex-linked disease caused by the absence of a clotting factor, so bleeding continues for a long time.

text: Photosynthesis in a plant cell takes place in the
explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps light energy for the manufacture of food.

text: The green pigment of plants that traps light energy is
explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly red and blue light and reflects green, giving leaves their colour.

text: The metal present in the chlorophyll molecule is
explanation: Chlorophyll has a magnesium atom at the centre of its porphyrin ring, in contrast to the iron in haemoglobin.

text: The loss of water in the form of vapour from the aerial parts of a plant is called
explanation: Transpiration takes place mainly through the stomata of leaves and helps draw water up the plant.

text: Water and mineral salts are conducted in a plant by the
explanation: Xylem vessels carry water and dissolved minerals upwards from the roots to the leaves.

text: The minute pores in a leaf through which gases are exchanged are called
explanation: Each stoma is bounded by two guard cells that open and close the pore.

text: Bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of leguminous plants belong to the genus
explanation: Rhizobium lives symbiotically in the root nodules of legumes and converts atmospheric nitrogen into usable compounds.

text: The plant hormone chiefly responsible for cell elongation in shoots is
explanation: Auxin promotes elongation of cells behind the shoot tip; the other three are animal hormones.

text: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from
explanation: In the light reaction, water is split into hydrogen and oxygen, and it is this oxygen that escapes.

text: Water enters the root hairs of a plant mainly by the process of
explanation: Soil water passes through the root hair membrane into the more concentrated cell sap by osmosis.

text: The chief source of energy in a normal human diet is
explanation: Carbohydrates supply most of the body's energy, providing about four kilocalories per gram.

text: The nutrients mainly required for the growth and repair of body tissues are
explanation: Proteins supply the amino acids from which new tissue and enzymes are built.

text: Kwashiorkor in children is caused by the deficiency of
explanation: Kwashiorkor follows a diet badly short of protein and shows swelling of the limbs and abdomen.

text: Which food component supplies the greatest amount of energy per gram?
explanation: Fat yields about nine kilocalories per gram, roughly twice as much as carbohydrate or protein.

text: The roughage of the human diet consists mainly of
explanation: Cellulose from plant foods cannot be digested by man but adds bulk that keeps the bowel moving.

text: The chemical symbol of sodium is
explanation: Sodium takes its symbol Na from its Latin name natrium; Ni is the symbol for nickel.

text: The chemical symbol of potassium is
explanation: Potassium is denoted K after its Latin name kalium; P stands for phosphorus and Pt for platinum.

text: The chemical symbol Fe stands for
explanation: Fe comes from ferrum, the Latin name of iron; fluorine is F and francium is Fr.

text: The chemical symbol of gold is
explanation: Gold is written Au from the Latin aurum; Ag is silver and Gd is gadolinium.

text: The chemical symbol Pb belongs to
explanation: Pb is taken from plumbum, the Latin name of lead, which also gives us the word plumbing.

text: The chemical symbol of tin is
explanation: Tin is Sn from the Latin stannum; Ti is titanium and Te is tellurium.

text: The chemical symbol Hg is used for
explanation: Mercury is Hg from hydrargyrum, meaning liquid silver.

text: The most abundant element in the Earth's crust is
explanation: Oxygen makes up roughly 46 per cent of the crust by mass, mainly locked up in silicate and oxide minerals.

text: The most abundant element in the universe is
explanation: Hydrogen accounts for about three quarters of the ordinary matter of the universe by mass.

text: The most abundant metal in the Earth's crust is
explanation: Aluminium is the commonest metal of the crust at about 8 per cent by mass, ahead of iron.

text: The modern periodic law arranges elements in order of increasing
explanation: Properties of elements are periodic functions of atomic number, which resolved the anomalies of the mass-based table.

text: The scientist who established that the properties of elements depend on atomic number was
explanation: Henry Moseley's X-ray studies showed atomic number, not atomic mass, is the fundamental ordering property.

text: Elements of Group 1 of the periodic table are known as
explanation: Lithium, sodium, potassium and their congeners form strongly alkaline hydroxides and are called alkali metals.

text: Fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine together form the group called
explanation: Group 17 elements are the halogens, a name meaning salt-formers.

text: Helium, neon, argon and krypton belong to the group called
explanation: These Group 18 elements have complete outer electron shells and are chemically very unreactive.

text: The number of periods in the modern periodic table is
explanation: The table has seven horizontal rows, each period corresponding to the filling of a principal energy level.

text: The number of groups in the long form of the periodic table is
explanation: The long form has eighteen vertical columns numbered 1 to 18.

text: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of
explanation: Atomic number is defined as the count of protons; the sum of protons and neutrons is the mass number.

text: Isotopes of the same element differ from one another in the number of
explanation: Isotopes share the same proton number but carry different numbers of neutrons, so their mass numbers differ.

text: The most electronegative element is
explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of all elements, about 4.0 on the Pauling scale.

text: The lanthanide and actinide series of elements belong to the
explanation: In these two inner transition series the differentiating electron enters an f orbital, so they form the f-block.

text: The only metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature is
explanation: Mercury melts at about minus 39 degrees Celsius and so is liquid at room temperature; bromine is a non-metal.

text: The only non-metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature is
explanation: Bromine is a dense reddish-brown liquid; iodine is solid and chlorine is a gas at room temperature.

text: The gas used to fill airships and weather balloons because it is light and non-inflammable is
explanation: Helium has very low density but, unlike hydrogen, does not burn, so it is preferred for lifting balloons.

text: Ordinary incandescent electric bulbs are usually filled with
explanation: Argon is inert and cheap, so it protects the hot tungsten filament from burning away.

text: The gas that gives a bright red-orange glow in advertisement discharge tubes is
explanation: Neon emits the familiar red-orange light in discharge tubes, which is why such signs are called neon signs.

text: The approximate percentage of nitrogen in dry air by volume is
explanation: Dry air is about 78 per cent nitrogen and 21 per cent oxygen by volume.

text: The pH of pure water at 25 degrees Celsius is
explanation: Pure water is neutral because the concentrations of hydrogen and hydroxide ions are equal, giving pH 7.

text: Blue litmus paper dipped in an acidic solution turns
explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red, while bases turn red litmus blue.

text: The acid that gives vinegar its sour taste is
explanation: Vinegar is a dilute aqueous solution of acetic acid, usually about 5 to 8 per cent.

text: The acid found in lemons and other citrus fruits is
explanation: Citric acid is the dominant organic acid of citrus fruits and gives them their sharp taste.

text: Souring of milk into curd is caused by the formation of
explanation: Bacteria ferment lactose into lactic acid, which lowers the pH and curdles the milk protein.

text: The irritation caused by an ant sting is due to
explanation: Ants inject formic acid, which takes its name from formica, the Latin word for ant.

text: The acid used as electrolyte in a lead storage battery is
explanation: A lead-acid accumulator uses dilute sulphuric acid between lead and lead dioxide plates.

text: Aqua regia, which dissolves gold, is a mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid in the ratio
explanation: Aqua regia is three parts concentrated hydrochloric acid to one part concentrated nitric acid by volume.

text: Caustic soda is the common name of
explanation: Sodium hydroxide is called caustic soda because it corrodes skin and other organic matter.

text: Milk of magnesia, taken as an antacid, is a suspension of
explanation: Magnesium hydroxide is a mild base that neutralises excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach.

text: The chemical formula of common table salt is
explanation: Table salt is sodium chloride, an ionic compound of sodium and chlorine.

text: Baking soda is chemically known as
explanation: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3, which releases carbon dioxide on heating and makes dough rise.

text: Washing soda is chemically
explanation: Washing soda is Na2CO3.10H2O, the hydrated form of sodium carbonate used to soften water for laundry.

text: The acid used for etching designs on glass is
explanation: Hydrofluoric acid attacks silica in glass, forming silicon tetrafluoride, so it is used for etching.

text: The chemical formula of limestone is
explanation: Limestone, marble and chalk are all forms of calcium carbonate, CaCO3.

text: Quicklime, obtained by strongly heating limestone, is
explanation: Heating calcium carbonate drives off carbon dioxide and leaves calcium oxide, CaO, called quicklime.

text: Slaked lime has the formula
explanation: Adding water to quicklime gives calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2, known as slaked lime.

text: Plaster of Paris is obtained by the controlled heating of
explanation: Gypsum, calcium sulphate dihydrate, loses most of its water at about 120 degrees Celsius to give plaster of Paris.

text: Blue vitriol is the common name of
explanation: Hydrated copper sulphate, CuSO4.5H2O, forms blue crystals and is called blue vitriol.

text: Laughing gas, used as a mild anaesthetic, is
explanation: Nitrous oxide, N2O, produces a euphoric effect on inhalation, hence the name laughing gas.

text: Dry ice is the solid form of
explanation: Solid carbon dioxide sublimes directly to gas without wetting anything, so it is called dry ice.

text: The chemical formula of ammonia is
explanation: Ammonia is NH3, a pungent gas in which nitrogen is bonded to three hydrogen atoms.

text: The chemical formula of methane is
explanation: Methane, the first member of the alkane series, has one carbon bonded to four hydrogen atoms.

text: Ozone is an allotrope of oxygen having the formula
explanation: Ozone consists of three oxygen atoms per molecule and forms the protective layer in the stratosphere.

text: Rust formed on iron is chemically
explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3.xH2O, produced when iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of moisture.

text: Among metals, the best conductor of electricity is
explanation: Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of all metals, though copper is used in wiring because it is cheaper.

text: The most malleable and ductile metal is
explanation: Gold can be beaten into extremely thin leaf and drawn into very fine wire, exceeding all other metals.

text: The metal with the lowest density is
explanation: Lithium has a density of about 0.53 grams per cubic centimetre, the lowest of any metal.

text: The hardest naturally occurring substance is
explanation: Diamond, a form of carbon with a rigid three-dimensional network of covalent bonds, tops the Mohs scale at 10.

text: Sodium metal is stored under
explanation: Sodium reacts violently with water and moist air, so it is kept under kerosene, with which it does not react.

text: Rusting of iron takes place only in the presence of
explanation: Both air and moisture are needed; iron does not rust in dry air or in air-free water.

text: Galvanisation protects iron by coating it with a layer of
explanation: Zinc is more reactive than iron and corrodes in its place, giving sacrificial protection.

text: The non-metal that conducts electricity and is used to make electrodes is
explanation: In graphite each carbon uses only three of its four valence electrons for bonding, leaving delocalised electrons that carry current.

text: The chief ore from which aluminium is extracted is
explanation: Bauxite, a hydrated aluminium oxide, is purified to alumina and then electrolysed to obtain aluminium.

text: Haematite is an important ore of
explanation: Haematite is ferric oxide, Fe2O3, and is the principal ore smelted in blast furnaces to make iron.

text: Cinnabar is an ore of
explanation: Cinnabar is mercuric sulphide, HgS, the main natural source of mercury.

text: Brass is an alloy of
explanation: Brass is made mainly of copper with zinc added, which makes it harder and more workable than pure copper.

text: Bronze is an alloy of
explanation: Bronze is copper alloyed with tin, historically the first alloy widely used for tools and weapons.

text: Steel is an alloy of iron with
explanation: Ordinary steel is iron containing a small controlled percentage of carbon, which greatly increases its strength.

text: The element added to steel to make it stainless is
explanation: Chromium forms a thin adherent oxide film on the surface that stops further corrosion.

text: Ordinary soft solder used in electrical work is an alloy of
explanation: Solder is mainly tin and lead, a combination chosen for its low melting point.

text: German silver is an alloy of
explanation: Despite its name German silver contains no silver at all; it is copper, zinc and nickel.

text: The chief constituent of the alloy duralumin is
explanation: Duralumin is largely aluminium with small amounts of copper, magnesium and manganese, and is used in aircraft.

text: An amalgam is an alloy in which one component is always
explanation: By definition an amalgam is an alloy of mercury with another metal, as in dental fillings.

text: The chief constituent of compressed natural gas is
explanation: Natural gas and the CNG made from it are about 90 per cent methane.

text: Liquefied petroleum gas used in domestic cylinders is mainly a mixture of
explanation: LPG consists chiefly of butane and propane, which liquefy easily under moderate pressure.

text: Crude petroleum is separated into petrol, kerosene and diesel by
explanation: The fractions have different boiling ranges and are drawn off at different heights of a fractionating column.

text: The octane number of a fuel is a measure of its
options: Ignition quality in a diesel engine
Resistance to knocking in a petrol engine
explanation: A higher octane number means the petrol resists premature ignition, or knocking, in the engine cylinder.

text: Water gas is a mixture of
explanation: Passing steam over red-hot coke gives carbon monoxide and hydrogen, together called water gas.

text: The main combustible constituent of biogas is
explanation: Anaerobic digestion of organic waste yields a gas that is mostly methane, with carbon dioxide as the main diluent.

text: The fuel with the highest calorific value per kilogram is
explanation: Hydrogen releases roughly 150 kilojoules per gram on burning, far more than any hydrocarbon fuel.

text: Incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels produces the poisonous gas
explanation: With insufficient oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, which binds haemoglobin and blocks oxygen transport.

text: The variety of coal with the highest carbon content is
explanation: Anthracite is the most mature coal, containing over 90 per cent carbon, and burns with almost no smoke.

text: The monomer from which polythene is made is
explanation: Polythene is formed by addition polymerisation of ethene molecules under heat and pressure.

text: The plastic abbreviated PVC is
explanation: PVC stands for polyvinyl chloride, made from vinyl chloride and used for pipes, cables and sheets.

text: Bakelite, used for electrical switches, is an example of a
explanation: Bakelite sets permanently on moulding into a cross-linked network and cannot be softened again by heating.

text: The chemical name of Teflon, used for non-stick coatings, is
explanation: Teflon is polytetrafluoroethylene, whose strong carbon-fluorine bonds make it inert and slippery.

text: Nylon belongs to the class of polymers called
explanation: Nylon chains are joined by amide linkages, the same type of bond found in proteins.

text: Vulcanisation of rubber is carried out by heating it with
explanation: Sulphur forms cross-links between rubber chains, making the rubber harder, stronger and less sticky.

text: The chemical formula of urea is
explanation: Urea, CO(NH2)2, is made industrially from ammonia and carbon dioxide and is the world's commonest nitrogen fertiliser.

text: The approximate nitrogen content of urea fertiliser is
explanation: Urea contains about 46 per cent nitrogen by mass, the highest of any solid nitrogen fertiliser.

text: In fertiliser grading, the letters NPK stand for
explanation: N, P and K are the three major plant nutrients supplied by mixed fertilisers.

text: The fertiliser DAP supplies plants with
explanation: DAP is diammonium phosphate, so it provides both nitrogen and phosphorus.

text: Ammonia is manufactured on an industrial scale by the
explanation: The Haber process combines nitrogen and hydrogen at high pressure over an iron catalyst to give ammonia.

text: The catalyst used in the Haber process is
explanation: Finely divided iron, with promoters, catalyses the combination of nitrogen and hydrogen into ammonia.

text: Muriate of potash used as a fertiliser is chemically
explanation: Muriate of potash is potassium chloride, KCl, the cheapest and most widely used potassium fertiliser.

text: Sulphuric acid is manufactured industrially by the
explanation: In the contact process sulphur dioxide is oxidised to sulphur trioxide over a catalyst and then absorbed to give sulphuric acid.

text: Sodium carbonate is manufactured industrially by the
explanation: The Solvay or ammonia-soda process makes sodium carbonate from brine, limestone and ammonia.

text: Nitric acid is manufactured industrially by the
explanation: The Ostwald process oxidises ammonia over a platinum catalyst to nitrogen oxides, which are absorbed in water to give nitric acid.

text: Electrolysis of concentrated brine yields caustic soda, hydrogen and
explanation: In the chlor-alkali process chloride ions are oxidised at the anode to chlorine gas.

text: The principal raw material used in the manufacture of ordinary glass is
explanation: Glass is made by fusing silica sand with soda ash and limestone, silica being the main ingredient.

text: Chlorofluorocarbons released from refrigerators and aerosols are harmful because they destroy
explanation: Chlorine atoms released from CFCs by ultraviolet light break ozone molecules apart in the stratosphere.

text: Bleaching powder is prepared by passing chlorine over
explanation: Chlorine passed over dry calcium hydroxide gives bleaching powder, used for disinfecting and bleaching.

text: Hardness of water is caused mainly by the dissolved salts of
explanation: Calcium and magnesium ions react with soap to form an insoluble scum, which is what makes water hard.

text: Temporary hardness of water is due to the presence of
explanation: Dissolved calcium and magnesium bicarbonates decompose on heating, which is why this hardness is called temporary.

text: Temporary hardness of water can be removed simply by
explanation: Boiling decomposes the bicarbonates into insoluble carbonates that settle out as scale.

text: Municipal drinking water is commonly disinfected by adding
explanation: Chlorine kills bacteria and leaves a residual that protects the water in the distribution network.

text: Water has its maximum density at
explanation: Water is densest at 4 degrees Celsius, which is why ice floats and ponds freeze from the top down.

text: Heavy water, used as a moderator in nuclear reactors, is
explanation: Heavy water is D2O, in which ordinary hydrogen is replaced by its heavier isotope deuterium.

text: Electrolysis of acidified water gives hydrogen and oxygen in a volume ratio of
explanation: Since water is H2O, twice as much hydrogen as oxygen is liberated by volume.

text: Hard water is unsuitable for washing because it
options: Does not readily form lather with soap
explanation: Calcium and magnesium ions precipitate soap as an insoluble scum instead of producing lather.

text: A controlled amount of fluoride is added to drinking water or toothpaste to prevent
explanation: Fluoride strengthens tooth enamel against acid attack and so reduces tooth decay.

text: Which is the largest planet in the solar system?
explanation: Jupiter's diameter is about eleven times that of Earth, making it larger than all the other planets combined.

text: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
explanation: Iron oxide dust on the Martian surface gives Mars its characteristic reddish colour.

text: Which planet has the highest surface temperature?
explanation: Venus has a dense carbon dioxide atmosphere that traps heat, giving surface temperatures near 460 degrees Celsius even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

text: Which planet is tilted almost on its side, with an axial tilt of about 98 degrees?
explanation: Uranus rotates with its axis nearly in the plane of its orbit, so its poles alternately face the Sun.

text: Which planet takes about 243 Earth days to complete one rotation on its axis?
explanation: Venus has the slowest rotation of any planet, and it also rotates in a retrograde direction.

text: Which is the largest natural satellite in the solar system?
explanation: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is larger than the planet Mercury.

text: Which moon of Saturn has a dense atmosphere rich in nitrogen?
explanation: Titan is the only moon known to have a thick atmosphere, composed mainly of nitrogen with some methane.

text: Which body lost its status as a planet when the International Astronomical Union redefined the term in 2006?
explanation: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet because it has not cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit.

text: The asteroid belt lies between the orbits of which two planets?
explanation: The main asteroid belt occupies the region between Mars and Jupiter.

text: Which is the largest object in the asteroid belt?
explanation: Ceres contains roughly a quarter of the belt's total mass and is classified as a dwarf planet.

text: The energy radiated by the Sun is produced by
explanation: Hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium in the Sun's core, releasing energy according to mass-energy equivalence.

text: The visible surface of the Sun is called the
explanation: The photosphere is the layer from which sunlight escapes into space, at a temperature of about 5,500 degrees Celsius.

text: Light from the Sun takes approximately how long to reach the Earth?
explanation: At about 150 million kilometres and a light speed of 300,000 km per second, sunlight takes roughly 8 minutes 20 seconds.

text: Which star is nearest to the Sun?
explanation: Proxima Centauri lies about 4.24 light years away, closer than any other known star.

text: A fragment of rock from space that survives its passage through the atmosphere and lands on Earth is called a
explanation: A meteoroid becomes a meteor while burning in the atmosphere and is called a meteorite once it reaches the ground.

text: A solar eclipse occurs when
options: the Earth's shadow falls on the Sun
the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
the Sun comes between the Earth and the Moon
the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
explanation: During a solar eclipse the Moon blocks sunlight and casts its shadow on part of the Earth's surface.

text: A lunar eclipse can occur only at the phase of
explanation: Only at full moon is the Earth positioned directly between the Sun and the Moon so that its shadow can fall on the Moon.

text: The same face of the Moon is always turned towards the Earth because
options: the Moon does not rotate at all
the Moon orbits in the plane of the ecliptic
the Earth's gravity stops lunar rotation
the Moon's rotation period equals its period of revolution
explanation: This synchronous rotation means the Moon turns once on its axis in exactly the time it takes to orbit the Earth.

text: Ocean tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the
explanation: Although the Sun also contributes, the Moon is far closer and exerts roughly twice the tide-raising force.

text: Spring tides, the highest tides of the month, occur at
explanation: At new and full moon the Sun, Earth and Moon are aligned, so their tide-raising forces add together.

text: Who was the first human being to travel into space?
explanation: Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth aboard Vostok 1 in April 1961.

text: Who was the first person to set foot on the Moon?
explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface during the Apollo 11 mission.

text: The seasons on Earth are caused by
options: the changing distance of the Earth from the Sun
the rotation of the Earth on its axis
the tilt of the Earth's axis together with its revolution
explanation: Because the axis stays tilted at a fixed angle as the Earth orbits, each hemisphere receives more direct sunlight for part of the year.

text: The Earth's axis is inclined to the plane of its orbit at an angle of about
explanation: This tilt of roughly 23.5 degrees from the vertical produces the annual cycle of seasons.

text: The summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere falls on about
explanation: On 21 June the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer, giving the Northern Hemisphere its longest day.

text: The Tropic of Cancer lies at a latitude of
explanation: The Tropic of Cancer marks the northern limit at which the Sun can be directly overhead.

text: The lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere is the
explanation: The troposphere extends from the surface to about 8-16 km and contains almost all weather phenomena.

text: The ozone layer is located in the
explanation: Ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere at heights of roughly 15 to 35 kilometres.

text: Most meteors entering the Earth's atmosphere burn up in the
explanation: Friction with the increasingly dense air of the mesosphere vaporises most incoming meteoroids.

text: Which region of the atmosphere reflects radio waves back to the Earth, making long-distance radio communication possible?
explanation: Ionised gas layers in the ionosphere bend and reflect radio waves back towards the surface.

text: Which gas is present in the largest proportion in dry air?
explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78 per cent of dry air by volume.

text: Oxygen forms approximately what percentage of dry air by volume?
explanation: Oxygen accounts for roughly 21 per cent of dry air, the second most abundant constituent after nitrogen.

text: The boundary separating the troposphere from the stratosphere is called the
explanation: The tropopause marks the level at which the fall of temperature with height in the troposphere ceases.

text: Which is the third most abundant gas in dry air?
explanation: Argon makes up about 0.93 per cent of dry air, more than carbon dioxide or any other trace gas.

text: Atmospheric pressure is measured with a
explanation: A barometer measures the weight of the column of air above it, usually in millibars or millimetres of mercury.

text: In the Northern Hemisphere, winds circulating around a low-pressure centre blow
explanation: The Coriolis deflection to the right in the Northern Hemisphere makes air spiral anticlockwise into a cyclone.

text: The Coriolis effect, which deflects winds and ocean currents, is a consequence of
options: unequal heating of land and sea
the Earth's revolution around the Sun
explanation: Because the Earth spins beneath moving air, winds appear deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern.

text: Which cloud type is associated with thunderstorms and heavy showers?
explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds are tall vertical clouds produced by strong convection and bring thunder, lightning and heavy rain.

text: Lines joining places receiving equal amounts of rainfall are called
explanation: Isohyets are used on climatic maps to show the distribution of precipitation.

text: Jet streams are fast-moving air currents found in the
explanation: Jet streams flow near the tropopause, at heights of roughly 9 to 12 kilometres.

text: El Nino refers to the abnormal warming of surface waters in the
explanation: El Nino is a periodic warming of the eastern and central equatorial Pacific that disturbs weather patterns worldwide.

text: The summer monsoon rains of Pakistan and India are brought by winds blowing from the
explanation: Moisture-laden south-west monsoon winds blow from the Indian Ocean towards the heated land mass in summer.

text: The belt of calm, light and variable winds lying near the equator is known as the
explanation: Intense heating at the equator causes air to rise rather than blow horizontally, producing a zone of calms.

text: Granite is an example of which type of rock?
explanation: Granite crystallises slowly from magma deep below the surface, making it a coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock.

text: Marble is formed by the metamorphism of
explanation: Heat and pressure recrystallise the calcite in limestone to produce marble.

text: Slate is a metamorphic rock formed from
explanation: Low-grade metamorphism of fine-grained shale produces slate, which splits into thin sheets.

text: Which mineral occupies the top position on the Mohs scale of hardness?
explanation: Diamond is rated 10 on the Mohs scale and can scratch every other mineral.

text: Which element is most abundant in the Earth's crust?
explanation: Oxygen forms roughly 46 per cent of the crust by weight, mostly combined in silicate minerals.

text: Which metal is most abundant in the Earth's crust?
explanation: Aluminium makes up about 8 per cent of the crust, more than any other metal.

text: Bauxite is the chief ore of
explanation: Bauxite is a hydrated aluminium oxide from which almost all commercial aluminium is extracted.

text: Cinnabar is the principal ore of
explanation: Cinnabar is mercuric sulphide and is roasted to obtain metallic mercury.

text: The Earth's core consists mainly of
explanation: Seismic evidence and meteorite composition indicate a core dominated by iron with about 5-10 per cent nickel.

text: Which layer accounts for the greatest share of the Earth's volume?
explanation: The mantle is about 2,900 kilometres thick and makes up roughly 84 per cent of the Earth's volume.

text: The boundary between the Earth's crust and the mantle is known as the
explanation: The Mohorovicic discontinuity, or Moho, is marked by a sudden increase in seismic wave velocity.

text: The Earth's magnetic field is generated chiefly in the
explanation: Convection currents of molten iron in the outer core act as a dynamo that produces the magnetic field.

text: The point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake is the
explanation: Shaking is generally strongest at the epicentre because it is nearest the source of the waves.

text: Which seismic waves travel fastest and are recorded first at a seismic station?
explanation: P waves are compressional waves and move faster than shear or surface waves, so they arrive first.

text: Which seismic waves cannot pass through liquids, providing evidence that the outer core is molten?
explanation: S waves are shear waves, and liquids cannot sustain shear stress, so they are blocked by the outer core.

text: Tsunamis are most commonly generated by
explanation: Sudden vertical displacement of the sea floor during a submarine earthquake sets off long-wavelength waves.

text: The theory of continental drift was put forward by
explanation: Wegener proposed in 1912 that the continents had once been joined and had since drifted apart.

text: The name given to the single supercontinent that is believed to have existed before the continents drifted apart is
explanation: Pangaea later split into Laurasia in the north and Gondwana in the south.

text: The Ring of Fire, a zone of frequent earthquakes and volcanoes, surrounds the
explanation: Subduction of oceanic plates around the margins of the Pacific produces this belt of volcanic and seismic activity.

text: Mid-ocean ridges are formed at
explanation: Where plates move apart, magma rises to fill the gap and creates new oceanic crust along a ridge.

text: The Himalayas were formed by the collision of the
explanation: The northward movement of the Indian plate into Eurasia crumpled the intervening sediments into fold mountains.

text: The San Andreas Fault in California is an example of a
explanation: At a transform boundary two plates slide horizontally past each other without creating or destroying crust.

text: The hypothesis of sea-floor spreading was proposed by
explanation: Harry Hess suggested in the early 1960s that new ocean floor forms at ridges and spreads outwards.

text: Which is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth?
explanation: The Pacific covers about a third of the Earth's surface and contains the deepest known trenches.

text: The deepest known point of the world's oceans lies in the
explanation: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench of the western Pacific reaches nearly 11,000 metres below sea level.

text: The average salinity of sea water is about
explanation: Sea water contains roughly 35 grams of dissolved salts per kilogram, that is 35 parts per thousand.

text: The most abundant salt dissolved in sea water is
explanation: Sodium chloride accounts for about 77 per cent of the dissolved solids in sea water.

text: Water covers approximately what fraction of the Earth's surface?
explanation: Oceans and seas cover close to 71 per cent of the planet's surface area.

text: The Gulf Stream is
options: a cold current of the Pacific Ocean
a cold current of the Indian Ocean
a warm current of the North Atlantic Ocean
a warm current of the Southern Ocean
explanation: The Gulf Stream carries warm water north-eastwards across the Atlantic and moderates the climate of north-west Europe.

text: Which gas is the largest single contributor to the human-induced greenhouse effect?
explanation: Carbon dioxide released by burning fossil fuels accounts for the greatest share of the added radiative forcing.

text: Greenhouse gases warm the lower atmosphere chiefly by absorbing
options: infrared radiation emitted by the Earth
explanation: They allow short-wave sunlight to pass through but absorb the long-wave infrared radiation given off by the warmed surface.

text: Without the natural greenhouse effect, the average surface temperature of the Earth would be about
explanation: Natural greenhouse warming raises the mean surface temperature from roughly minus 18 degrees Celsius to about 15 degrees Celsius.

text: Paddy fields, livestock and landfills are major sources of which greenhouse gas?
explanation: Methane is produced by anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in flooded soils, animal guts and waste dumps.

text: The chemical formula of ozone is
explanation: Ozone is a triatomic allotrope of oxygen.

text: The ozone layer protects life on Earth by absorbing
explanation: Stratospheric ozone absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet-B radiation before it reaches the surface.

text: Depletion of the ozone layer is caused mainly by
explanation: Chlorine atoms released from CFCs by ultraviolet light catalyse the destruction of ozone molecules.

text: The most severe seasonal thinning of the ozone layer is observed over
explanation: Extremely cold polar stratospheric clouds over Antarctica speed up the chlorine reactions that destroy ozone each spring.

text: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 deals with
options: substances that deplete the ozone layer
explanation: It obliged countries to phase out the production and use of CFCs, halons and other ozone-depleting chemicals.

text: The Kyoto Protocol, which set binding limits on greenhouse gas emissions, was adopted in
explanation: It was agreed at the third Conference of the Parties in Kyoto in December 1997 and came into force in 2005.

text: The Paris Agreement on climate change was adopted in
explanation: It was concluded at COP21 in Paris in December 2015 and entered into force the following year.

text: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change was opened for signature at the Earth Summit held in
explanation: The 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro produced the UNFCCC along with the Convention on Biological Diversity.

text: The first United Nations Conference on the Human Environment was held in Stockholm in
explanation: The 1972 Stockholm Conference led to the creation of the United Nations Environment Programme.

text: The Ramsar Convention is concerned with the conservation of
explanation: Signed in Ramsar, Iran, in 1971, it provides for the protection of wetlands of international importance.

text: CITES is an international agreement that regulates
explanation: The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species controls cross-border trade in threatened plants and animals.

text: The Basel Convention regulates the
explanation: It was adopted in 1989 to control the export of hazardous waste, particularly from developed to developing countries.

text: IPCC stands for
explanation: The IPCC was established by the World Meteorological Organization and UNEP to assess the science of climate change.

text: World Environment Day is observed every year on
explanation: The United Nations designated 5 June, the opening day of the 1972 Stockholm Conference, as World Environment Day.

text: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is observed on
explanation: It marks 16 September 1987, the day the Montreal Protocol was signed.

text: Acid rain is caused mainly by atmospheric emissions of
options: sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen
explanation: These gases dissolve in cloud droplets to form sulphuric and nitric acids that fall with the rain.

text: Rain is generally described as acid rain when its pH falls below about
explanation: Unpolluted rain is already slightly acidic at pH 5.6 because of dissolved carbon dioxide, so lower values indicate pollution.

text: Which pollutant from vehicle exhaust combines with haemoglobin and reduces the blood's capacity to carry oxygen?
explanation: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin far more strongly than oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin.

text: Photochemical smog is produced by the action of sunlight on
explanation: Sunlight drives reactions between nitrogen oxides and unburnt hydrocarbons to form ground-level ozone and other irritants.

text: PM2.5 in air-quality reports refers to particulate matter with a diameter smaller than
explanation: These fine particles are small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream.

text: Eutrophication of lakes and rivers is caused by an excess of
explanation: Nutrient runoff from fertilizers triggers algal blooms whose decay depletes dissolved oxygen in the water.

text: Biochemical oxygen demand is used as a measure of
explanation: BOD records the oxygen consumed by micro-organisms in breaking down organic matter, so a high value indicates heavy pollution.

text: Minamata disease resulted from poisoning by
explanation: Industrial discharge of methylmercury into Minamata Bay in Japan contaminated fish eaten by local people.

text: Itai-itai disease, marked by severe bone pain, was caused by poisoning with
explanation: Cadmium from mine waste entered rice fields in Japan and accumulated in the bones of those who ate the rice.

text: Blue baby syndrome in infants is associated with drinking water containing excess
explanation: Nitrate is converted to nitrite in the body and interferes with the oxygen-carrying ability of haemoglobin.

text: Excess fluoride in drinking water causes
explanation: Fluorosis mottles the teeth and, in severe cases, deforms the bones and joints.

text: The intensity of noise is measured in
explanation: The decibel is a logarithmic unit expressing sound level relative to a standard reference intensity.

text: Which of the following is a non-renewable source of energy?
explanation: Coal is a fossil fuel formed over millions of years and cannot be replaced on a human time scale.

text: A photovoltaic cell converts
explanation: Semiconductor materials in a solar cell release electrons when struck by photons, producing an electric current.

text: Geothermal energy is obtained from
explanation: Hot rocks and underground water heated by the Earth's internal heat are tapped to raise steam for turbines.

text: A wind turbine generates electricity from the
explanation: Moving air turns the blades, and the rotating shaft drives a generator that produces electricity.

text: Volcanic activity is most closely associated with which type of plate boundary in addition to divergent boundaries?
explanation: At convergent boundaries an oceanic plate is subducted, melts at depth and feeds volcanoes above the subduction zone.

text: The rigid outer shell of the Earth, made up of the crust and the uppermost mantle, is called the
explanation: The lithosphere is broken into the tectonic plates that move over the weaker asthenosphere below.

text: All poets are dreamers. All dreamers are optimists. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: Two universal affirmative premises linked by the middle term 'dreamers' yield the universal conclusion that every poet is an optimist.

text: No reptiles are mammals. All cobras are reptiles. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: Cobras fall entirely within the class of reptiles, and that class is wholly excluded from mammals, so no cobra can be a mammal.

text: Some students are athletes. All athletes are disciplined. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: The students who are athletes must share every property of athletes, so at least some students are disciplined; nothing is proved about the rest.

text: All squares are rectangles. Some rectangles are red. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: A particular affirmative statement can be converted, so 'some rectangles are red' gives 'some red things are rectangles'; the premises never link squares to colour.

text: All doctors are graduates. No graduate is illiterate. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: Doctors are contained in the class of graduates, and that class is entirely excluded from the illiterate, so no doctor is illiterate.

text: From the statement 'Some books are novels', which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: A particular affirmative proposition converts simply: if some books are novels then some novels are books.

text: From the statement 'No politician is honest', which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: No honest person is a politician
explanation: A universal negative proposition converts simply, so exclusion between the two classes holds in both directions.

text: Given 'All mangoes are fruits', which statement does NOT follow?
options: Whatever is not a fruit is not a mango
explanation: Reversing a universal affirmative is invalid; the other three are restatements or the contrapositive of the original.

text: All A are B. All B are C. All C are D. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: Class inclusion is transitive, so A is contained in B, B in C and C in D, placing every A inside D.

text: No red object is cheap. Some pens are red. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: The pens that are red belong to a class wholly excluded from cheap things, so at least those pens are not cheap.

text: All metals conduct electricity. Copper is a metal. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: An individual belonging to a class inherits every property asserted of the whole class.

text: Only members may enter the club. Bilal entered the club. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: 'Only members may enter' makes membership a necessary condition of entry, so anyone who entered must be a member.

text: Everyone who passes the test receives a certificate. Ahmed did not receive a certificate. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: Ahmed did not sit the test
Ahmed did not pass the test
explanation: This is modus tollens: denying the consequent of a conditional lets us deny its antecedent.

text: In a categorical syllogism, the term that appears in both premises but not in the conclusion is called the
explanation: The middle term links the two premises and is dropped from the conclusion; the major and minor terms are the predicate and subject of the conclusion.

text: The argument 'All dogs are animals; all cats are animals; therefore all dogs are cats' commits the fallacy of
explanation: The middle term 'animals' is not distributed in either premise, so the two classes are never actually connected.

text: An argument is valid when
options: the conclusion must be true if the premises are true
its conclusion happens to be true
its premises happen to be true
explanation: Validity is about the form of the inference: true premises cannot lead to a false conclusion in a valid argument.

text: A sound argument is one that
options: is valid and has all true premises
has a true conclusion but false premises
explanation: Soundness adds factual truth of the premises to formal validity.

text: All soldiers are brave. Some brave persons are poets. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: Only the second premise can be converted; nothing connects soldiers with poets because the middle term is undistributed.

text: No teacher is lazy. All lazy persons are unpunctual. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: No lazy person is a teacher
explanation: The first premise converts simply; the premises do not exclude teachers from the wider class of unpunctual persons.

text: All P are Q. No Q are R. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: Everything in P lies inside Q, and Q is wholly excluded from R, so P and R cannot overlap.

text: Some officers are engineers. All engineers are graduates. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: The officers who are engineers must also be graduates, which establishes a particular, not a universal, conclusion.

text: The proverb 'All that glitters is not gold' is logically intended to mean
options: Some things that glitter are not gold
explanation: The intended sense is the denial of a universal claim, which is a particular negative: not everything glittering is gold.

text: Which statement is logically equivalent to 'If it rains, the match is cancelled'?
options: If it does not rain, the match is not cancelled
The match is cancelled only if it rains
If the match is not cancelled, it did not rain
If the match is cancelled, it rained
explanation: A conditional is equivalent only to its contrapositive, formed by negating and interchanging antecedent and consequent.

text: The contrapositive of 'If a number is divisible by 4, then it is even' is
options: If a number is even, then it is divisible by 4
If a number is not divisible by 4, then it is not even
If a number is odd, then it is divisible by 4
If a number is not even, then it is not divisible by 4
explanation: The contrapositive negates both parts and reverses their order, and it always has the same truth value as the original.

text: The converse of 'If x is a bird, then x has feathers' is
options: If x has feathers, then x is a bird
If x is not a bird, then x has no feathers
If x has no feathers, then x is not a bird
x is a bird and x has feathers
explanation: The converse simply interchanges antecedent and consequent, and it does not follow from the original statement.

text: If a metal is heated it expands. This metal did not expand. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: The metal is not really a metal
explanation: Denying the consequent of a true conditional validly denies its antecedent (modus tollens).

text: 'If a student cheats he is disqualified. Aslam was disqualified, therefore Aslam cheated.' This reasoning commits the fallacy of
explanation: Disqualification may have other causes; inferring the antecedent from the consequent is invalid.

text: 'If it snows the road is closed. It did not snow, therefore the road is not closed.' This reasoning commits the fallacy of
explanation: The conditional says nothing about what happens when it does not snow, so the road may still be closed for another reason.

text: Either the fuse is blown or the bulb is dead. The fuse is not blown. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: The bulb is in working order
explanation: In a disjunctive syllogism, denying one alternative of a true disjunction establishes the other.

text: If P then Q, and if Q then R. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: If not P then not R
explanation: Conditionals chain together in a hypothetical syllogism, giving the transitive conditional from P to R.

text: 'Only if you submit the form will you be registered.' This statement means that submitting the form is
explanation: 'Only if' introduces a necessary condition; it does not promise that submission alone guarantees registration.

text: Passing the written test is a necessary but not sufficient condition for appointment. It follows that
options: nobody who fails the test is appointed
everyone who passes the test is appointed
only those who fail the test are appointed
the test has no bearing on appointment
explanation: A necessary condition must be met by every appointee, but meeting it does not by itself secure appointment.

text: The correct denial of the statement 'All students passed' is
options: At least one student did not pass
explanation: The contradictory of a universal affirmative is a particular negative, requiring only one exception.

text: The correct denial of the statement 'Some birds can swim' is
explanation: The contradictory of a particular affirmative is the universal negative covering every member of the class.

text: The expression 'if and only if' states
options: both a necessary and a sufficient condition
explanation: A biconditional asserts that each side implies the other, so the condition is both necessary and sufficient.

text: 'No pass, no entry' is logically equivalent to
options: A pass may be shown after entry
If a person enters, that person has a pass
If a person has a pass, that person enters
explanation: 'If no pass then no entry' is a conditional whose contrapositive is 'if entry then a pass'.

text: A conditional statement and its contrapositive are
options: equivalent only when both are false
explanation: Negating and interchanging the two parts preserves truth value in every case.

text: Either the report is wrong or the machine is faulty. The machine is not faulty. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: The machine must still be replaced
Both the report and the machine are in order
explanation: Eliminating one disjunct of a true disjunction leaves the other one standing.

text: A is taller than B. C is shorter than B. Who is the tallest of the three?
options: B and C are of equal height
explanation: A stands above B and B stands above C, so A occupies the top of the order.

text: P is heavier than Q, Q is heavier than R, and R is heavier than S. Who is the lightest?
explanation: The chain of comparisons runs P, Q, R, S from heaviest to lightest.

text: X is older than Y and Y is older than Z. Which statement must be true?
explanation: The 'older than' relation is transitive, so the order runs X, Y, Z from oldest to youngest.

text: In a race Ali finished ahead of Bilal, Bilal finished ahead of Danish, and Danish finished ahead of Ehsan. Who finished last?
explanation: The stated order is Ali, Bilal, Danish, Ehsan, so Ehsan is at the end of it.

text: Amina scored more than Bushra, and Chanda scored less than Bushra. Which statement must be true?
options: Bushra scored the highest of the three
explanation: Amina is above Bushra and Bushra is above Chanda, so Amina must be above Chanda.

text: All members of the committee are lawyers. Sana is not a lawyer. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: Sana is not a member of the committee
Sana is a member of the committee
Some lawyers are not committee members
explanation: Anyone outside the class of lawyers must lie outside the committee, which is contained in that class.

text: Every book on the shelf is in Urdu. This dictionary is in English. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: This dictionary is not on the shelf
This dictionary is on the shelf
explanation: An item lacking the property common to everything on the shelf cannot be on the shelf.

text: No student in the class is above 20 years of age. Kamran is 22 years old. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: Kamran is not a student anywhere
Some students in the class are 22
Kamran is not in the class
explanation: Kamran fails the age condition satisfied by every member of the class, so he cannot be a member.

text: All the pens in the box are blue. This pen is red. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: This pen did not come from the box
This pen came from the box
The box contains some red pens
explanation: Since every pen in the box is blue, a red pen must have some other source.

text: Aslam is sitting between Bashir and Chand, and Bashir is to Aslam's left. Which statement must be true?
options: Aslam is at one end of the row
explanation: Aslam has one neighbour on each side; with Bashir on the left, Chand must be on the right.

text: Five persons stand in a row. Q is exactly in the middle and P stands immediately to Q's left. How many persons stand to the left of P?
explanation: Q occupies the third place and P the second, so exactly one person stands to P's left.

text: Whenever it rains the road becomes wet. The road is dry today. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: Rain does not affect the road
explanation: If rain always produced a wet road, a dry road rules out rain (modus tollens).

text: All A are B. No B is C. Some C are D. Which conclusion must be true?
explanation: A lies wholly inside B and B is wholly outside C, so A and C cannot overlap; nothing follows about D.

text: A man says, 'All my sons are engineers.' Rashid is his son. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
explanation: A property asserted of every member of a group applies to any named member of it.

text: 'Do not accept his economic plan; he failed in his own business years ago.' This argument commits the fallacy of
explanation: The reasoning attacks the person's record instead of examining the merits of the plan itself.
