text: 'My opponent wants to reduce the defence budget, so clearly he wants the country left defenceless.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: The opponent's position is exaggerated into an absurd version that is easier to attack.

text: 'Nobody has ever proved that ghosts do not exist, so ghosts must exist.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: Absence of disproof is treated as proof, which the argumentum ad ignorantiam wrongly allows.

text: 'Millions of people buy this brand, so it must be the best.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: Widespread acceptance is not evidence of quality; the argumentum ad populum substitutes numbers for reasons.

text: 'Please raise my grade, sir; my family will be heartbroken if I fail.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: Sympathy is offered in place of any evidence that the grade was wrongly awarded.

text: 'Approve my proposal, or remember that your contract comes up for renewal next month.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: A veiled threat, not evidence, is used to secure agreement (argumentum ad baculum).

text: 'Either we abolish every subsidy or the economy will collapse.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: Only two extreme options are presented although many intermediate possibilities exist.

text: 'If students are allowed to retake one paper, they will soon demand to retake every paper and the examination system will collapse.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: A chain of increasingly serious consequences is asserted without any evidence that the first step leads to the last.

text: 'This law is just because it is right, and it is right because it is just.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: The conclusion is used as its own support, so the argument moves in a closed circle.

text: 'I wore my lucky shirt and the team won, so the shirt brought the victory.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: Mere sequence in time is mistaken for a causal connection.

text: 'I met two rude people from that city, so everyone there is rude.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: A sweeping conclusion is drawn from a sample far too small to support it.

text: 'Every player in the side is outstanding, so the side as a whole must be outstanding.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: Properties of the individual parts are transferred without warrant to the whole.

text: 'That is a very wealthy company, so every one of its employees must be wealthy.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: A property of the whole is wrongly assigned to each of its parts.

text: 'A feather is light; what is light cannot be dark; therefore a feather cannot be dark.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: The word 'light' shifts from meaning low in weight to meaning pale in colour within the same argument.

text: Asked about rising inflation, a speaker replies with a long description of the beauty of the northern areas. This is the fallacy of
explanation: An irrelevant subject is introduced to draw attention away from the question asked.

text: 'You advise me to give up smoking, but you smoke yourself, so your advice is worthless.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: The adviser's own conduct is irrelevant to whether the advice is correct; this is the 'you too' form of ad hominem.

text: 'A famous cricketer says this syrup cures diabetes, so it must cure diabetes.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: The person cited is respected in a field unrelated to medicine, so his endorsement is not evidence.

text: 'Running a country is exactly like running a household, so a government should never borrow money.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: The two cases differ in essential respects, so the comparison cannot carry the conclusion.

text: 'This practice must be wrong because it began during the colonial period.' This is the fallacy of
explanation: The argument judges an idea by its origin rather than by its present merits.

text: The fallacy of assuming that what is true of a whole must be true of each of its parts is called
explanation: Division moves from whole to parts; composition moves in the opposite direction, from parts to whole.

text: The fallacy of using the same word in two different senses within one argument is called
explanation: Equivocation trades on an ambiguity of a single term; amphiboly arises from ambiguous grammar instead.

text: The fallacy in which the conclusion is already assumed in the premises is known as
explanation: Petitio principii offers as support the very claim that is supposed to be proved.

text: The Latin phrase 'post hoc ergo propter hoc' means
options: after this, therefore because of this
explanation: It names the error of treating a later event as caused by an earlier one merely because it followed.

text: 'Argumentum ad hominem' literally means an argument directed
explanation: The attack is aimed at the person advancing the claim rather than at the claim itself.

text: 'Argumentum ad populum' is an appeal to
options: the beliefs or feelings of the crowd
explanation: It urges acceptance of a claim because many people already accept it.

text: 'Argumentum ad baculum' is an appeal to
explanation: 'Baculum' means a stick, so the phrase names the appeal to coercion rather than to evidence.

text: Statement: 'Take our tablet and your headache will disappear within ten minutes.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: People want quick relief from headache
Every tablet acts within ten minutes
Headache cannot be relieved in any other way
Our tablet is the cheapest available
explanation: The appeal only works if speed of relief is something the reader values; the other statements go far beyond what is taken for granted.

text: Statement: 'Boil the water before drinking it.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: Boiling improves the taste of water
All diseases are spread through water
Unboiled water may be unsafe to drink
explanation: The advice makes sense only if the water as supplied carries some risk that boiling removes.

text: Statement: 'The examination centre has been shifted to the college because more candidates applied this year.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: The old centre has been demolished
Candidates prefer colleges to other buildings
Examinations must always be held in colleges
The college can seat more candidates than the old centre
explanation: The stated reason works only if the new venue solves the problem of extra candidates, that is, it has greater capacity.

text: Statement: 'Submit the form before 5 p.m.; forms received later will not be accepted.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: Applicants are able to submit the form before 5 p.m.
No applicant will submit the form at all
The office remains closed during the day
explanation: Setting a deadline presupposes that those addressed are in a position to meet it.

text: Statement: 'In case of fire use the stairs; do not use the lift.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: Stairs are always wider than lifts
Fires break out only in tall buildings
Lifts are more expensive to run
The lift may become unsafe during a fire
explanation: The instruction rests on the belief that the lift carries a risk in a fire that the stairs do not.

text: Statement: 'Write your roll number on the answer sheet.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: Every candidate has been given a roll number
explanation: The instruction can be obeyed only if each candidate actually possesses a roll number.

text: Statement: 'The company has announced a bonus for workers in order to raise production.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: Production cannot be raised by any other means
explanation: The measure presupposes a link between extra pay and extra output; the other options are not needed for the plan to make sense.

text: Statement: 'Read the instructions on the packet before using this medicine.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: The medicine is dangerous in every dose
All users are trained in medicine
The instructions are printed in Urdu
explanation: The direction assumes the existence of instructions on the packet; nothing else is required for it to be sensible.

text: Statement: 'Because of the fuel shortage the government has advised offices to work four days a week.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: The shortage will last for ever
Working fewer days will reduce fuel consumption
explanation: The advice is a means to an end and presupposes that the shorter week actually saves fuel.

text: Statement: 'Buy a helmet and ride safely.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: Wearing a helmet makes riding safer
Riding without a helmet is impossible
explanation: The advertisement links the purchase to safety, which presupposes that the helmet contributes to it.

text: In the analysis of an argument, an assumption is
options: a definition of the terms used
something taken for granted but not stated
explanation: An assumption is an unstated premise that the argument needs in order to work.

text: Statement: 'Notice: all employees must attend the training session on Monday.' Which assumption is implicit in this statement?
options: Employees will be available on Monday
Employees know nothing about their work
explanation: A compulsory session presupposes that those required to attend can in fact be present that day.

text: Event A: the price of petrol was raised on Monday. Event B: taxi fares were increased on Tuesday. Which relation is most reasonable?
options: A is the cause and B is the effect
B is the cause and A is the effect
The two events are entirely unconnected
Both are effects of a fall in demand
explanation: Fuel is a direct input cost for taxis, and the increase in fares followed the rise in price.

text: Ice-cream sales and cases of heat stroke both rise sharply in June. The best explanation is that
options: heat stroke causes people to buy ice-cream
the two figures are recorded wrongly
both are effects of the hot weather
explanation: A third factor, high temperature, produces both trends, so the correlation between them is not causal.

text: The reasoning 'cities with more police also record more crime, therefore police cause crime' overlooks the principle that
options: correlation does not by itself establish causation
explanation: Two things may vary together because one drives the other in the reverse direction or because a third factor drives both.

text: A survey shows that students who sleep longer obtain higher marks. Which finding would most weaken the claim that extra sleep causes higher marks?
options: Sleep is necessary for good health
Well-organised students both sleep longer and study more effectively
explanation: It supplies a common third factor that could produce both the longer sleep and the better marks.

text: In a controlled experiment the purpose of the control group is
options: to reduce the cost of the experiment
to confirm what the researcher expects
to provide a comparison in which the suspected cause is absent
to increase the total number of participants
explanation: Only by comparing with a group not exposed to the factor can a change be attributed to that factor.

text: Event A: heavy rain fell throughout the night. Event B: the low-lying road was under water in the morning. Which relation is most reasonable?
options: B is the cause and A is the effect
Both are effects of an unrelated cause
There is no connection between them
A is the cause and B is the effect
explanation: The rain preceded the flooding and is sufficient to explain water collecting on low ground.

text: Which of the following is a necessary condition for ordinary combustion?
explanation: Ordinary burning cannot occur without an oxidising agent, whereas the particular fuel or the weather may vary.

text: 'Since the new mayor took office, road accidents have fallen.' Before crediting the mayor, one must first rule out
options: the geographical size of the city
the cost of building the roads
other changes such as new traffic rules or fewer vehicles on the road
explanation: A causal claim survives only when alternative explanations for the same change have been eliminated.

text: Question: should smoking be prohibited in enclosed public places? Which is the strongest argument?
options: No, because some people enjoy it
Yes, because the smoke inhaled by others damages their health
No, because smokers also pay taxes
explanation: An argument is strong when it is relevant and rests on a substantial consequence, here harm to non-smokers.

text: Question: should public transport fares be subsidised? Which of the following arguments is weak?
options: No, because the transport minister is personally unpopular
Yes, because low fares help low-income commuters
No, because subsidies enlarge the fiscal deficit
Yes, because cheaper transport reduces the use of private cars
explanation: An argument that turns on a person rather than on the policy is irrelevant and therefore weak.

text: A strong argument is one that is
options: held by a large number of people
relevant to the issue and supported by evidence
explanation: Strength depends on relevance and evidential support, not on length, popularity or the speaker's fame.

text: Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that wearing seat belts should be compulsory?
options: Seat belts are made of strong woven fabric
Most new cars are fitted with seat belts
Several other countries have such a law
Seat belts sharply reduce deaths in road accidents
explanation: Direct evidence that the measure saves lives supports the case, while the other statements are merely incidental.

text: Which of the following, if true, most weakens the claim that a town's new filtration plant has made its water safe?
options: The plant was inaugurated by a senior official
A few residents continue to buy bottled water
Tests taken after installation still show bacteria above the permitted limit
The plant cost more than was estimated
explanation: Test results bearing directly on water quality contradict the claim; cost, ceremony and habit do not.

text: An argument that offers only emotional appeal and no supporting evidence is best described as
explanation: Without relevant evidence an argument fails to support its conclusion, however moving it may be.

text: In evaluating arguments, 'relevance' means that the argument
options: is short and easy to read
bears directly on the question under discussion
explanation: A relevant argument addresses the actual issue; irrelevant material cannot support the conclusion however true it is.

text: Statement: cracks have appeared in a bridge carrying heavy traffic on a national highway. Which course of action is most appropriate?
options: Wait until the cracks widen further
Ban all vehicles throughout the province
Close the bridge to traffic and have it inspected at once
Raise the toll charged on the bridge
explanation: The immediate danger to life requires the traffic to be stopped and the structure examined; the other steps are irrelevant or excessive.

text: Statement: an outbreak of dengue fever has been reported in a city. Which course of action is most appropriate?
options: Close all schools in the country permanently
Prohibit the sale of mosquito nets
Shift the population of the city elsewhere
Remove stagnant water and spray the affected localities
explanation: Dengue spreads through mosquitoes that breed in standing water, so removing breeding sites attacks the cause.

text: Statement: an unusually large number of candidates failed a departmental examination this year. Which course of action is most appropriate?
options: Examine the reasons for the poor result and arrange remedial training
explanation: Finding the cause before acting is the reasonable step; the other options either avoid the problem or punish without evidence.

text: Statement: a public office receives repeated complaints about long queues at its counters. Which course of action is most appropriate?
options: Reduce the working hours of the office
Close half of the existing counters
Introduce an appointment and token system and open more counters at peak hours
explanation: Managing the flow of visitors addresses the cause of the queues, while the other measures would worsen the situation.

text: Statement: a school reports that many pupils arrive without breakfast and lose attention in class. Which course of action is most appropriate?
options: Start a school meal scheme and inform parents of the problem
Expel the pupils who lose attention
explanation: Providing food and involving parents removes the stated cause of inattention; the other steps punish the pupils instead.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Punjab, Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar?
explanation: Karachi, Lahore and Peshawar are cities, while Punjab is a province.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Iron, Copper, Bronze, Aluminium?
explanation: Copper, iron and aluminium are pure metallic elements; bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Rose, Mango, Lily, Jasmine?
explanation: Rose, lily and jasmine are flowers; mango is a fruit.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Eye, Ear, Nose, Lung?
explanation: Eye, ear and nose are sense organs; the lung is a respiratory organ.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Sparrow, Emu, Ostrich, Kiwi?
explanation: Ostrich, emu and kiwi are flightless birds; the sparrow can fly.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Square, Rectangle, Triangle, Rhombus?
explanation: Square, rectangle and rhombus have four sides; the triangle has three.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Litre, Metre, Gallon, Pint?
explanation: Litre, gallon and pint measure volume; the metre measures length.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Karakoram?
explanation: Indus, Jhelum and Chenab are rivers; Karakoram is a mountain range.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Cotton, Wheat, Rice, Maize?
explanation: Wheat, rice and maize are food grains; cotton is a fibre crop.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: April, June, August, September?
explanation: April, June and September have 30 days each; August has 31.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Mercury, Moon, Venus, Mars?
explanation: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets; the Moon is a natural satellite.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Hammer, Screwdriver, Saw, Nail?
explanation: Hammer, saw and screwdriver are tools; a nail is a fastener worked on by tools.

text: Which one does not belong to the group: Sahara, Amazon, Nile, Danube?
explanation: Nile, Amazon and Danube are rivers; the Sahara is a desert.

text: Which number does not belong to the group: 3, 5, 9, 7?
explanation: 3, 5 and 7 are prime numbers, while 9 is composite (3 x 3).

text: Which number does not belong to the group: 8, 100, 27, 64?
explanation: 8, 27 and 64 are perfect cubes of 2, 3 and 4; 100 is not a perfect cube.

text: Which number does not belong to the group: 49, 64, 81, 80?
explanation: 49, 64 and 81 are the squares of 7, 8 and 9; 80 is not a perfect square.

text: Which number does not belong to the group: 21, 17, 13, 19?
explanation: 13, 17 and 19 are prime; 21 is divisible by 3 and 7.

text: Which number does not belong to the group: 15, 25, 42, 35?
explanation: 15, 25 and 35 are multiples of 5; 42 is not.

text: Which number does not belong to the group: 4, 20, 16, 8?
explanation: 4, 8 and 16 are powers of 2; 20 is not.

text: Which number does not belong to the group: 121, 144, 169, 180?
explanation: 121, 144 and 169 are the squares of 11, 12 and 13; 180 is not a perfect square.

text: Doctor is to Patient as Lawyer is to:
explanation: A doctor renders professional service to a patient just as a lawyer does to a client.

text: Pen is to Write as Knife is to:
explanation: The pair links an instrument with its function: a pen is used to write, a knife to cut.

text: Bird is to Nest as Bee is to:
explanation: The relation is creature to its dwelling: a bird lives in a nest, a bee in a hive.

text: Foot is to Shoe as Hand is to:
explanation: A shoe is the covering worn on the foot, as a glove is the covering worn on the hand.

text: Cat is to Kitten as Dog is to:
explanation: The relation is adult to young: a young cat is a kitten and a young dog is a puppy.

text: Teacher is to School as Judge is to:

explanation: All three are polygons bounded by straight sides, and a hexagon is a six-sided polygon.

text: Which letter comes next in the series A, D, G, J, ?
explanation: Each letter moves forward 3 places (positions 1, 4, 7, 10), so the next is position 13 = M.

text: Which letter comes next in the series Z, X, V, T, ?
explanation: The letters move backward 2 places each time (26, 24, 22, 20), so the next is position 18 = R.

text: Which letter comes next in the series A, B, D, G, K, ?
explanation: The gaps grow +1, +2, +3, +4, so the next gap is +5 and K (11) + 5 = position 16 = P.

text: Which letter comes next in the series Z, W, T, Q, ?
explanation: The letters move back 3 places each time (26, 23, 20, 17), so the next is position 14 = N.

text: Which letter comes next in the series A, E, I, M, ?
explanation: Each letter moves forward 4 places (positions 1, 5, 9, 13), so the next is position 17 = Q.

text: Which letter comes next in the series W, S, O, K, ?
explanation: The letters move back 4 places each time (23, 19, 15, 11), so the next is position 7 = G.

text: Which letter comes next in the series A, Z, B, Y, C, X, ?
explanation: The series alternates between the start of the alphabet (A, B, C, D) and the end (Z, Y, X), so the next term is D.

text: Which letter comes next in the series Z, Y, X, W, ?
explanation: The alphabet is running backwards one letter at a time, so the letter after W is V.

text: Which letter comes next in the series A, C, F, J, O, ?
explanation: The gaps are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6 and O (15) + 6 = position 21 = U.

text: Which letter comes next in the series J, F, M, A, M, J, ?
explanation: These are the first letters of the months January to June, so the next is July = J.

text: Which letter comes next in the series O, T, T, F, F, S, S, ?
explanation: These are the first letters of One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Six, Seven, so the next is Eight = E.

text: Which term comes next in the series AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
explanation: The first letters run forward A, B, C, D, E while the second run backward Z, Y, X, W, V, so the next pair is EV.

text: Which term comes next in the series AB, DE, GH, JK, ?
explanation: Each pair starts 3 letters after the previous pair (A, D, G, J, M) and takes the next letter with it, so the next pair is MN.

text: Which term comes next in the series AC, EG, IK, MO, ?
explanation: Both letters advance 4 places each step (A, E, I, M, Q and C, G, K, O, S), so the next pair is QS.

text: Which term comes next in the series A1, B2, C3, D4, ?
explanation: The letters advance one place and the numbers rise by 1, so the next term is E5.

text: Which term comes next in the series A1, C3, E5, G7, ?
explanation: Each letter is paired with its position in the alphabet and only odd positions are used, so the next term is I9.

text: Which term comes next in the series Z26, Y25, X24, W23, ?
explanation: Each letter is paired with its alphabet position, counting backwards from Z, so the next term is V22.

text: Which term comes next in the series A2, D4, G6, J8, ?
explanation: The letters advance 3 places (A, D, G, J, M) while the numbers rise by 2, so the next term is M10.

text: Which term comes next in the series B1, D4, F9, H16, ?
explanation: The letters advance 2 places (B, D, F, H, J) while the numbers are the squares 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, so the next term is J25.

text: Which term comes next in the series A1, B3, C5, D7, ?
explanation: The letters advance one place while the numbers are consecutive odd numbers, so the next term is E9.

text: Which term comes next in the series 2A, 4C, 6E, 8G, ?
explanation: The numbers rise by 2 and the letters advance 2 places, so the next term is 10I.

text: Which term comes next in the series Z5, X10, V20, T40, ?
explanation: The letters move back 2 places (Z, X, V, T, R) while the numbers double, so the next term is R80.

text: Which term comes next in the series A5, C10, E15, G20, ?
explanation: The letters advance 2 places (A, C, E, G, I) while the numbers rise by 5, so the next term is I25.

text: Which term comes next in the series Z1, X2, V3, T4, ?
explanation: The letters move back 2 places (Z, X, V, T, R) while the numbers count up by 1, so the next term is R5.

text: What is the SI unit of force?
explanation: One newton is the force that gives a mass of one kilogram an acceleration of one metre per second squared.

text: The SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature is the
explanation: Kelvin is one of the seven SI base units; Celsius and Fahrenheit are derived or non-SI temperature scales.

text: The SI unit of frequency is the
explanation: One hertz corresponds to one complete cycle or vibration per second.

text: Electrical resistance is measured in
explanation: A conductor has a resistance of one ohm when a potential difference of one volt drives a current of one ampere through it.

text: Which of the following is a base quantity in the SI system?
explanation: Luminous intensity, measured in candela, is one of the seven SI base quantities; the others listed are derived quantities.

text: A light year is a unit of
explanation: A light year is the distance travelled by light in vacuum in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometres.

text: One horsepower is approximately equal to
explanation: The mechanical horsepower is defined as about 746 watts of power.

text: The commercial unit of electrical energy used on domestic bills is the
explanation: Electricity meters record energy in kilowatt-hours, where one kilowatt-hour equals 3.6 million joules.

text: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
explanation: Displacement specifies both how far and in which direction, so it is a vector; the others have magnitude only.

text: The instrument used to measure the humidity of air is the
explanation: A hygrometer indicates the amount of water vapour present in the air.

text: Wind speed is measured by an
explanation: An anemometer, usually a set of rotating cups, measures the speed of the wind.

text: In a circuit, an ammeter is always connected
options: between the live and neutral wires
explanation: An ammeter has very low resistance and must carry the whole current, so it is joined in series.

text: A screw gauge is chiefly used to measure
options: the diameter of a thin wire
explanation: A screw gauge, or micrometer, measures very small thicknesses and diameters to a fraction of a millimetre.

text: The relative density of a liquid is measured with a
explanation: A hydrometer floats at a depth that depends on the density of the liquid, and the scale reads relative density directly.

text: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the law of
explanation: The first law states that a body keeps its state of rest or uniform motion unless an external force acts, which is the property of inertia.

text: The relation F = ma is a statement of Newton's
explanation: The second law states that the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force, giving F = ma for constant mass.

text: The backward recoil of a gun when it is fired is explained by the
explanation: The total momentum before firing is zero, so the forward momentum of the bullet is balanced by an equal backward momentum of the gun.

text: The momentum of a moving body is the product of its
explanation: Linear momentum is defined as mass multiplied by velocity, and it is a vector quantity.

text: The acceleration due to gravity near the surface of the Earth is about
explanation: The standard value of g at the Earth's surface is 9.8 metres per second squared.

text: The value of the acceleration due to gravity on Earth is greatest at
explanation: The Earth is flattened at the poles, so the surface there is nearer the centre and g is largest.

text: The weight of an object on the Moon is about
options: one-sixth of its weight on Earth
one-third of its weight on Earth
equal to its weight on Earth
six times its weight on Earth
explanation: Gravity on the Moon is roughly one-sixth of that on Earth, so the same mass weighs about one-sixth as much.

text: A body moving in a circle at constant speed has an acceleration directed
options: towards the centre of the circle
away from the centre of the circle
opposite to the direction of motion
explanation: The velocity changes direction continuously, and the resulting centripetal acceleration always points towards the centre.

text: The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is approximately
explanation: A body must be projected at about 11.2 kilometres per second to escape the Earth's gravitational pull.

text: The orbital period of a geostationary satellite is
explanation: A geostationary satellite completes one orbit in 24 hours so that it keeps pace with the Earth's rotation and appears fixed in the sky.

text: According to Newton's law of gravitation, the force between two bodies is inversely proportional to
options: the square of the distance between them
the cube of the distance between them
explanation: Gravitational attraction follows an inverse square law, falling to one quarter when the separation is doubled.

text: The work done by a force is zero when the angle between the force and the displacement is
explanation: Work equals force times displacement times the cosine of the angle, and cosine of 90 degrees is zero.

text: One joule of work is done when a force of one newton moves a body through
explanation: The joule is defined as one newton-metre, the work done by a force of one newton acting over a distance of one metre.

text: The kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with speed v is given by
explanation: Kinetic energy equals one half of the mass multiplied by the square of the speed.

text: If the speed of a moving car is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes
explanation: Kinetic energy is proportional to the square of the speed, so doubling the speed multiplies the energy by four.

text: Water stored in a dam at a height possesses mainly
explanation: Because of its raised position the water holds gravitational potential energy, which converts to kinetic energy as it falls.

text: The law of conservation of energy states that energy
options: is always increasing in the universe
can be created but not destroyed
can neither be created nor destroyed but only changed in form
explanation: Energy can only be transformed from one form to another; the total energy of an isolated system stays constant.

text: An electric generator converts
explanation: A generator rotates a coil in a magnetic field, so mechanical work is turned into electrical energy by induction.

text: An electric motor converts electrical energy mainly into
explanation: Current in a coil placed in a magnetic field experiences a turning force, producing mechanical rotation.

text: The mechanical advantage of a machine is the ratio of
explanation: Mechanical advantage is the load overcome divided by the effort applied; the ratio of outputs to inputs of work is the efficiency.

text: A wheelbarrow is an example of a lever of the
explanation: In a wheelbarrow the load lies between the fulcrum at the wheel and the effort at the handles, which defines a second-class lever.

text: The chief advantage of a single fixed pulley is that it
options: changes the direction of the effort
halves the load to be lifted
explanation: A single fixed pulley has a mechanical advantage of one, so it only lets the effort be applied downward instead of upward.

text: A screw may be regarded as a modified form of
explanation: The thread of a screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder.

text: The efficiency of an actual machine is always less than 100 per cent because
options: the load is always greater than the effort
some energy is wasted against friction
energy is destroyed inside the machine
the mechanical advantage is always less than one
explanation: Part of the work input is converted into heat by friction, so the useful work output is smaller than the input.

text: Absolute zero of temperature corresponds to
explanation: Zero kelvin, the lowest possible temperature, is about -273 degrees Celsius.

text: A temperature of 27 degrees Celsius is equal to
explanation: Kelvin temperature is obtained by adding 273 to the Celsius reading, so 27 + 273 = 300 K.

text: The Celsius and Fahrenheit scales show the same numerical reading at
explanation: Solving C = (9C/5) + 32 gives C = -40, the single temperature at which both scales agree.

text: Heat travels through a solid metal rod mainly by
explanation: In solids energy passes from particle to particle without bulk movement of matter, which is conduction.

text: Heat reaches the Earth from the Sun by the process of
explanation: Radiation is the only mode of heat transfer that needs no material medium, so it can cross the vacuum of space.

text: Which metal is the best conductor of heat?
explanation: Silver has the highest thermal conductivity of all metals, slightly above copper.

text: The specific heat capacity of water is about
explanation: About 4200 joules are needed to raise the temperature of one kilogram of water by one kelvin, an unusually high value.

text: Water has its maximum density at a temperature of
explanation: Water contracts on cooling only down to 4 degrees Celsius and then expands, so it is densest at that temperature.

text: Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because the increased pressure
options: lowers the boiling point of water
increases the specific heat of water
raises the boiling point of water
reduces the latent heat of steam
explanation: Higher pressure inside the cooker allows water to boil above 100 degrees Celsius, so cooking proceeds at a higher temperature.

text: Evaporation of a liquid always produces
options: a rise in temperature of the remaining liquid
an increase in the mass of the liquid
explanation: The fastest molecules escape first and carry away energy, lowering the average energy and hence the temperature of what remains.

text: A bimetallic strip bends on heating because the two metals
explanation: The metal with the larger coefficient of linear expansion lengthens more, forcing the strip to curve.

text: Sound waves travelling through air are
explanation: Air particles vibrate back and forth along the direction of travel, producing compressions and rarefactions.

text: Sound cannot travel through
explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium, so it cannot pass through a vacuum.

text: The speed of sound in air at 0 degrees Celsius is about
explanation: Sound travels through air at roughly 332 metres per second at freezing point and slightly faster as the air warms.

text: Sound travels fastest in
explanation: Solids are the most elastic and closely packed media, so sound waves pass through them most rapidly.

text: The normal range of audible frequencies for a healthy human ear is
explanation: Frequencies below 20 hertz are infrasonic and those above 20,000 hertz are ultrasonic, both inaudible to humans.

text: An echo is produced by the
explanation: Sound bouncing back from a distant hard surface reaches the listener after a delay and is heard as a separate sound.

text: The pitch of a musical note depends on its
explanation: A higher frequency of vibration is perceived as a higher pitch.

text: The intensity level of sound is commonly measured in
explanation: The decibel is a logarithmic unit used to compare sound intensity levels.

text: SONAR, used to find the depth of the sea, works by sending out
explanation: SONAR emits ultrasonic pulses and times their echo from the sea bed to calculate depth.

text: The apparent rise in the pitch of a train whistle as the train approaches a listener is called the
explanation: Relative motion between source and observer changes the observed frequency, an effect named after Christian Doppler.

text: The speed of light in vacuum is about
explanation: Light travels at approximately 300,000 kilometres per second, that is 3 × 10^8 metres per second.

text: Light from the Sun takes about how long to reach the Earth?
explanation: The Sun is about 150 million kilometres away, so its light takes roughly eight minutes and twenty seconds to arrive.

text: The image formed by a plane mirror is always
options: virtual and of the same size as the object
explanation: A plane mirror forms an upright virtual image as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, and of equal size.

text: The rear-view mirror of a motor vehicle is
explanation: A convex mirror always gives an erect diminished image and covers a wider field of view behind the vehicle.

text: Refraction of light occurs because light
options: changes its speed in going from one medium to another
changes its colour in a new medium
is absorbed by the second medium
explanation: A change of speed at the boundary makes the ray bend unless it strikes the surface normally.

text: The refractive index of water is about
explanation: Light travels about 1.33 times more slowly in water than in vacuum; 1.5 is typical of glass and 2.42 of diamond.

text: Optical fibres transmit light signals over long distances by means of
explanation: Light striking the core-cladding boundary beyond the critical angle is reflected entirely back into the core.

text: The splitting of white light into its component colours by a glass prism is called
explanation: Different colours have different refractive indices in glass, so they emerge at different angles as a spectrum.

text: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
explanation: Red light lies at the long wavelength end of the visible spectrum and violet at the short wavelength end.

text: The blue colour of the clear daytime sky is caused by
options: absorption of red light by ozone
refraction of light in the atmosphere
scattering of sunlight by air molecules
explanation: Short wavelengths are scattered far more strongly by tiny air molecules, so scattered blue light reaches the eye from all directions.

text: The image formed on the retina of the human eye is
explanation: The eye lens converges light to form a real inverted image on the retina, which the brain interprets as upright.

text: Short-sightedness, or myopia, is corrected by using
explanation: A diverging concave lens moves the image back onto the retina for a myopic eye that focuses light in front of it.

text: The power of a lens is measured in
explanation: Lens power is the reciprocal of the focal length in metres and its unit is the dioptre.

text: The three primary colours of light are
explanation: Red, green and blue light combine in different proportions to produce all other colours, including white.

text: Which of the following electromagnetic radiations has the shortest wavelength?
explanation: Gamma rays lie at the extreme high-frequency end of the electromagnetic spectrum and so have the shortest wavelength.

text: X-rays were discovered by
explanation: Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and received the first Nobel Prize in Physics for the work.

text: Ohm's law is expressed by the relation
explanation: For a conductor at constant temperature the potential difference equals the current multiplied by the resistance.

text: The resistance of a metallic wire of uniform material
options: depends only on the current through it
does not depend on its length
explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area.

text: Domestic electrical appliances are connected to the mains supply
explanation: Parallel connection gives every appliance the same full voltage and lets each be switched on or off independently.

text: The wire used in an electric fuse should have
options: a high melting point and low resistance
a low melting point and high resistance
a high melting point and high resistance
a low melting point and zero resistance
explanation: A fuse wire must heat up quickly and melt before the excessive current can damage the circuit.

text: Which element is widely used as a semiconductor in electronic devices?
explanation: Silicon has a conductivity between that of conductors and insulators and forms the basis of diodes, transistors and chips.

text: The magnitude of the charge on an electron is about
explanation: The elementary charge is 1.6 × 10^-19 coulomb; 9.1 × 10^-31 kilogram is the electron's mass.

text: The direction of conventional current in a circuit is
options: the same as the direction of electron flow
undefined in a direct current circuit
always from negative to positive outside the cell
opposite to the direction of electron flow
explanation: Conventional current is taken to flow from the positive to the negative terminal, whereas electrons drift the other way.

text: The filament of an ordinary electric bulb is made of
explanation: Tungsten has a very high melting point and high resistivity, so it glows brightly without melting.

text: A transformer can work only with
options: both direct and alternating current equally
explanation: A transformer depends on a continuously changing magnetic flux, which only alternating current can provide.

text: The working of an electric generator is based on the principle of
explanation: Faraday showed that an electromotive force is induced whenever the magnetic flux linked with a coil changes.

text: When two like poles of magnets are brought close together, they
explanation: Like magnetic poles repel while unlike poles attract.

text: A bar magnet suspended freely so that it can turn will finally come to rest pointing
explanation: The Earth's magnetic field turns the magnet until its poles line up roughly along the north-south direction.

text: The core of an electromagnet is usually made of soft iron because soft iron
options: loses its magnetism as soon as the current stops
explanation: Soft iron is easily magnetised and demagnetised, which is exactly what a temporary electromagnet requires.

text: The neutron was discovered by
explanation: Chadwick identified the uncharged nuclear particle in 1932 and was awarded the Nobel Prize for it.

text: The existence of the atomic nucleus was established by the alpha particle scattering experiment performed under
explanation: Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed that the atom's positive charge and nearly all its mass are concentrated in a tiny nucleus.

text: The mass number of an atom is the total number of
explanation: Protons and neutrons are the nucleons, and together they account for almost the whole mass of the atom.

text: An alpha particle is identical with the nucleus of an atom of
explanation: An alpha particle consists of two protons and two neutrons, which is a helium nucleus.

text: Of the three main types of nuclear radiation, the most penetrating is
explanation: Gamma rays are uncharged electromagnetic waves and need thick lead or concrete to be stopped, while alpha is stopped by paper.

text: Radioactivity was first discovered by
explanation: Becquerel found in 1896 that uranium salts emitted penetrating radiation without any external stimulus.

text: The half-life of a radioactive element is the time in which
explanation: Half-life is the time taken for half the radioactive nuclei present in a sample to disintegrate.

text: Archimedes' principle states that a body immersed in a fluid experiences an upthrust equal to the
explanation: The loss in apparent weight of the body equals the weight of the fluid it pushes aside.

text: Hydraulic brakes in vehicles work on the principle stated by
explanation: Pascal's law says pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions, so a small force at the pedal produces a large force at the wheels.

text: The density of pure water is about
explanation: One cubic metre of water has a mass of about 1000 kilograms, that is one gram per cubic centimetre.

text: Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level supports a mercury column of
explanation: Normal atmospheric pressure balances a column of mercury 760 millimetres, or 76 centimetres, high.

text: The lift on the wing of an aeroplane in flight is explained by
explanation: Air moves faster over the curved upper surface, lowering the pressure there, and the pressure difference produces upward lift.

text: The mass of an electron is roughly what fraction of the mass of a proton?
explanation: A proton is about 1836 times heavier than an electron.

text: Friction between two sliding surfaces can be reduced by
options: increasing the load pressing them together
increasing the area of contact only
explanation: A lubricant forms a thin layer that keeps the surfaces apart and lowers the force of sliding friction.

text: The pressure exerted by a solid block on the ground can be reduced by
options: increasing the weight of the block
tilting the block on one edge
explanation: Pressure is force divided by area, so spreading the same weight over a larger area lowers the pressure.

text: According to Newton's third law of motion, action and reaction are equal and opposite but
options: cancel each other out on one body
act only when the bodies are in contact
explanation: Because the two forces act on different bodies they never cancel, which is why motion can result.

text: The force of gravity acting on a body is called its
explanation: Weight is a force measured in newtons and equals mass multiplied by the acceleration due to gravity.

text: A steel ship floats on water although steel is denser than water because
options: the ship is hollow and displaces a large weight of water
steel becomes lighter in sea water
sea water has a lower density than fresh water
the engines push the ship upward
explanation: The hollow hull makes the average density of the ship less than that of water, so the upthrust can balance its weight.

text: Which part of a computer is called the brain of the computer?
explanation: The CPU carries out the instructions of a program by performing arithmetic, logic and control operations, so it directs all other components.

text: In a CPU, ALU stands for
explanation: The Arithmetic Logic Unit performs all arithmetic calculations and logical comparisons inside the processor.

text: Which of the following is an example of system software?
explanation: An operating system manages hardware and provides a platform for application programs, which is the defining role of system software.

text: BIOS in a computer stands for
explanation: The Basic Input Output System is firmware that initialises hardware during start-up and hands control to the operating system.

text: In computing, GUI stands for
explanation: A Graphical User Interface lets users interact with a computer through icons, windows and menus instead of typed commands.

text: Who is known as the father of the computer?
explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine and the Analytical Engine, the first mechanical general-purpose computer concept.

text: The first generation of computers used which component for switching?
explanation: First-generation machines such as ENIAC and UNIVAC relied on vacuum tubes, which were bulky and generated great heat.

text: A compiler differs from an interpreter in that a compiler
options: translates the source program line by line at run time
converts machine code back into source code
executes the program without any translation
translates the entire source program before execution
explanation: A compiler translates the whole source program into object code in one pass, whereas an interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time.

text: An assembler is a program that converts
explanation: An assembler translates mnemonic assembly-language instructions into the binary machine code of a particular processor.

text: The main printed circuit board of a computer to which all other components connect is the
explanation: The motherboard carries the processor socket, memory slots, buses and connectors that link every other component.

text: One byte is equal to how many bits?
explanation: A byte is a group of eight binary digits and is the standard unit used to represent one character of data.

text: One kilobyte is conventionally equal to
explanation: Computer memory is measured in powers of two, so one kilobyte equals 2 to the power 10, that is 1024 bytes.

text: A group of four bits is called a
explanation: Half a byte, that is four bits, is termed a nibble and corresponds to exactly one hexadecimal digit.

text: One terabyte is equal to
explanation: The sequence of binary storage units rises by a factor of 1024, so 1 TB equals 1024 GB.

text: RAM is described as volatile memory because it
options: can only be read and never written
loses its contents when power is switched off
stores data permanently on magnetic platters
is located outside the computer case
explanation: Random Access Memory needs a constant power supply to retain data, so its contents vanish when the machine is switched off.

text: Which of the following memories has the fastest access time?
explanation: Cache memory sits closest to the processor and is built from high-speed static RAM, so it is accessed far faster than any secondary storage.

text: The storage capacity of a standard single-layer DVD is approximately
explanation: A single-sided, single-layer DVD holds about 4.7 gigabytes, roughly seven times the capacity of a CD.

text: Which of the following is an input device?
explanation: A scanner converts printed images and text into digital data and feeds it into the computer, which makes it an input device.

text: OMR technology is chiefly used to read
options: marks made in bubbles on answer sheets
explanation: Optical Mark Recognition detects the presence of pencil marks in fixed positions, which is why it is used to grade multiple-choice answer sheets.

text: OCR in computing stands for
explanation: Optical Character Recognition converts scanned images of printed or typed text into machine-editable characters.

text: Which of the following is an impact printer?
explanation: A dot matrix printer forms characters by striking pins against an inked ribbon and the paper, so it works by physical impact.

text: Which device functions as both an input and an output device?
explanation: A touch screen displays information like a monitor and simultaneously accepts user input through touch, serving both roles.

text: The smallest addressable element of an image on a computer display is called a
explanation: A pixel, short for picture element, is the smallest dot of the display grid whose colour and brightness can be controlled.

text: Printer resolution is normally measured in
explanation: Dots per inch expresses how many separate ink or toner dots a printer can place along one inch, which determines print sharpness.

text: The World Wide Web was invented by
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee proposed and built the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989, creating HTML, HTTP and the first browser.

text: HTTP stands for
explanation: Hypertext Transfer Protocol is the application-layer protocol used by web browsers and servers to exchange web pages.

text: HTML is best described as
options: an operating system for web servers
a markup language for creating web pages
explanation: Hypertext Markup Language uses tags to define the structure and content of web pages displayed by browsers.

text: In the context of the internet, URL stands for
explanation: A Uniform Resource Locator is the complete address that identifies where a resource is located on the web.

text: FTP is a protocol used primarily for
options: transferring files between computers over a network
explanation: File Transfer Protocol defines how files are uploaded to and downloaded from a remote server over a TCP/IP network.

text: SMTP is the standard protocol used for
explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol governs the sending and relaying of email messages between mail servers.

text: LAN stands for
explanation: A Local Area Network connects computers within a limited area such as one office building or campus.

text: The Domain Name System (DNS) performs the function of
options: translating domain names into IP addresses
explanation: DNS acts as the directory of the internet, converting human-readable names such as fpsc.gov.pk into numeric IP addresses.

text: An IPv4 address consists of how many bits?
explanation: IPv4 uses a 32-bit address written as four decimal octets separated by dots, allowing about 4.3 billion addresses.

text: An IPv6 address is how many bits long?
explanation: IPv6 expanded the address space to 128 bits, written as eight groups of hexadecimal digits, to overcome IPv4 exhaustion.

text: The network device used to connect two or more different networks and forward packets between them is a
explanation: A router examines the destination IP address of each packet and chooses the best path to forward it to another network.

text: The word modem is derived from
explanation: A modem modulates digital data onto an analogue carrier for transmission and demodulates the incoming signal back into digital form.

text: The OSI reference model consists of how many layers?
explanation: The Open Systems Interconnection model has seven layers, from the physical layer up to the application layer.

text: Wi-Fi wireless networking is defined by which IEEE standard family?
explanation: The IEEE 802.11 family of standards specifies wireless local area networking, marketed under the name Wi-Fi.

text: Which network is regarded as the forerunner of the modern internet?
explanation: ARPANET, funded by the US Department of Defense in 1969, was the first packet-switching network and evolved into the internet.

text: In a star topology, all the nodes of the network are connected to
explanation: Star topology links every node by its own cable to a central hub or switch, through which all communication passes.

text: The default port number used by HTTPS is
explanation: Secure web traffic over TLS is carried on port 443, while unencrypted HTTP uses port 80.

text: Which file extension belongs to an MS Excel workbook created in Excel 2007 or later?
explanation: Excel 2007 introduced the Open XML workbook format, saved with the .xlsx extension.

text: A file with the extension .pptx is opened by which program?
explanation: The .pptx extension identifies a PowerPoint presentation stored in the Open XML format.

text: In Windows, a file with the extension .exe is a
explanation: An .exe file contains machine instructions that Windows can load and run directly as a program.

text: PDF stands for
explanation: Portable Document Format, developed by Adobe, preserves a document's layout and fonts across different devices and platforms.

text: Which extension indicates a file containing plain unformatted text?
explanation: A .txt file stores only characters with no formatting information, and can be opened by any text editor.

text: The default file extension of a document created in MS Word 2007 and later versions is
explanation: From Word 2007 onward the default save format is Office Open XML, which uses the .docx extension.

text: In MS Excel, every formula entered in a cell must begin with
explanation: Excel recognises an entry as a formula only when it starts with the = sign, otherwise it treats it as text.

text: In MS Excel, a file that contains one or more worksheets is called a
explanation: The Excel document as a whole is a workbook, and each page of rows and columns inside it is a worksheet.

text: In MS Word, the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Z performs which action?
explanation: Ctrl + Z reverses the most recent action, and repeated presses step further back through the edit history.

text: In MS PowerPoint, pressing the F5 key
options: starts the slide show from the first slide
explanation: F5 launches the presentation in full-screen slide show mode beginning with the first slide.

text: Which MS Office application is a database management program?
explanation: MS Access stores data in related tables and provides queries, forms and reports, making it the Office database program.

text: Which MS Excel function adds all the numbers in a specified range of cells?
explanation: The SUM function returns the arithmetic total of the values in the range supplied as its argument.

text: In an MS Excel worksheet, columns are identified by
explanation: Excel labels columns with letters A, B, C onwards and rows with numbers, so a cell reference such as B4 combines both.

text: The MS Word feature used to produce many personalised letters from a single template and a list of recipients is called
explanation: Mail Merge combines a main document with a data source so that each copy of the letter carries a different name and address.

text: A self-replicating malicious program that spreads across a network without attaching itself to another program is called a
explanation: A worm is standalone malware that copies itself from computer to computer over a network, unlike a virus which needs a host file.

text: A Trojan horse is malware that
options: disguises itself as a useful program to gain entry
physically damages the hard disk platters
duplicates itself endlessly in memory only
explanation: A Trojan appears to be legitimate software and tricks the user into installing it, after which it performs hidden harmful actions.

text: Sending fraudulent emails that appear to come from a bank in order to steal a user's password is called
explanation: Phishing uses deceptive messages that imitate a trusted organisation to persuade victims to reveal login or financial details.

text: A firewall in a computer network is used to
options: increase the clock speed of the processor
control incoming and outgoing network traffic
explanation: A firewall filters traffic against a set of security rules, allowing authorised packets and blocking unauthorised ones.

text: Encryption is the process of converting
options: plaintext into an unreadable coded form
source code into an executable file
explanation: Encryption applies an algorithm and a key to turn readable data into ciphertext that only an authorised holder of the key can decode.

text: Malicious software that locks or encrypts a victim's files and demands payment to restore access is known as
explanation: Ransomware holds data hostage by encrypting it and displays a demand for payment in exchange for the decryption key.

text: Unsolicited bulk email sent to a large number of recipients is called
explanation: Spam is unwanted email sent indiscriminately in bulk, usually for advertising or as a vehicle for scams.

text: A denial of service attack aims to
options: steal encryption keys from a database
alter the domain registration of a website
install a hidden keylogger on every client
make a server or service unavailable to legitimate users
explanation: A DoS attack floods a system with excessive requests or traffic so that genuine users can no longer be served.

text: Two-factor authentication improves security because it requires
options: two different antivirus programs to be installed
the password to be changed twice a year
two independent forms of evidence to verify identity
explanation: Two-factor authentication combines something the user knows with something the user has or is, so a stolen password alone is not enough.

text: A small text file that a website stores on a visitor's computer to remember information about the visit is called a
explanation: Cookies are small data files written by a website to the browser so that preferences and session details persist between visits.

text: RADAR stands for
explanation: RADAR is an acronym for Radio Detection and Ranging, describing its use of radio waves to locate objects and measure distance.

text: SONAR is used mainly to detect objects under water because it employs
explanation: Sound waves travel efficiently through water while radio waves are strongly absorbed, so SONAR uses acoustic pulses and their echoes.

text: LASER stands for
options: Light Absorption by Sequential Emission of Rays
Linear Amplification of Standard Electromagnetic Radiation
Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation
Luminous Alignment of Spectral Energy Rays
explanation: The acronym describes the physical process by which the device produces an intense beam, namely stimulated emission of radiation.

text: Laser light differs from ordinary light chiefly because it is
explanation: The waves in a laser beam are in phase and of a single wavelength, which is why the beam stays narrow over long distances.

text: The operation of a laser depends on which phenomenon?
explanation: Stimulated emission, predicted by Einstein, causes an excited atom to emit a photon identical in phase and direction to the incident photon.

text: Holography, the technique of producing three-dimensional images, requires a source of
explanation: Holograms are recorded by the interference of two beams, which demands the highly coherent light that only a laser provides.

text: Optical fibres transmit light signals over long distances on the principle of
explanation: Light striking the core-cladding boundary beyond the critical angle is reflected entirely back into the core and so travels along the fibre.

text: In an optical fibre, the refractive index of the core compared with that of the cladding is
explanation: The core must be optically denser than the cladding for total internal reflection to occur and confine the light inside the core.

text: The medical instrument used to view internal organs, which relies on optical fibres, is the
explanation: An endoscope uses bundles of optical fibres to carry light into a body cavity and return the image to the observer.

text: The first artificial satellite launched into space was
explanation: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957, beginning the space age.

text: The orbital period of a geostationary satellite is approximately
explanation: A geostationary satellite completes one orbit in the same time the Earth takes to rotate once, so it appears fixed above one point.

text: A geostationary satellite orbits at a height of about
explanation: Only at roughly 35,800 km above the equator does the orbital period match the Earth's rotation, keeping the satellite stationary in the sky.

text: The first satellite launched by Pakistan was
explanation: Badr-1, an experimental communications satellite built by SUPARCO, was placed in orbit in July 1990.

text: SUPARCO is the national organisation of Pakistan responsible for
explanation: The Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, established in 1961, runs Pakistan's space and satellite programme.

text: GPS stands for
explanation: The Global Positioning System is a satellite constellation that lets a receiver compute its exact location from timing signals.

text: Nuclear power stations generate electricity from which nuclear process?
explanation: Reactors split heavy nuclei such as uranium-235 in a controlled chain reaction, and the heat released raises steam to drive turbines.

text: Which isotope is the usual fuel for a chain reaction in nuclear reactors?
explanation: Uranium-235 is the naturally occurring isotope that undergoes fission readily with slow neutrons, sustaining a chain reaction.

text: The function of a moderator in a nuclear reactor is to
options: absorb excess neutrons and stop the reaction
remove heat from the reactor core
explanation: Materials such as graphite and heavy water reduce neutron speed so that the neutrons are more likely to cause further fission.

text: Control rods in a nuclear reactor are made of materials such as cadmium and boron because these
options: reflect neutrons back into the core
explanation: Cadmium and boron capture free neutrons, so inserting the rods reduces the number available for fission and slows the reaction.

text: Heavy water used in some nuclear reactors is chemically
explanation: Heavy water is D2O, in which ordinary hydrogen is replaced by its heavier isotope deuterium, making it an efficient moderator.

text: The first nuclear power plant of Pakistan was established at
explanation: The Karachi Nuclear Power Plant, KANUPP, began operating in 1972 and was Pakistan's first commercial nuclear power station.

text: Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in May 1998 at
explanation: The tests were conducted in the Ras Koh hills of the Chagai district of Balochistan on 28 May 1998.

text: The double helix structure of DNA was proposed in 1953 by
explanation: Watson and Crick, using X-ray diffraction data, described DNA as two complementary strands wound into a double helix.

text: Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult body cell, was a
explanation: Dolly the sheep was produced at the Roslin Institute in 1996 by transferring the nucleus of an adult udder cell into an egg cell.

text: The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a technique used to
explanation: PCR uses repeated heating and cooling cycles with a DNA polymerase to make millions of copies of a chosen DNA segment.

text: In genetic engineering, restriction enzymes are described as molecular scissors because they
options: cut DNA at specific base sequences
explanation: Each restriction endonuclease recognises a particular short sequence and cuts the DNA there, allowing genes to be isolated.

text: Human insulin for the treatment of diabetes is now produced commercially by
options: chemical synthesis from amino acids in bulk
explanation: The human insulin gene is inserted into bacteria such as E. coli, which then manufacture the hormone by recombinant DNA technology.

text: Tissue culture is a biotechnological technique in which
options: whole plants are grown from small pieces of tissue in a nutrient medium
animal organs are preserved by freezing
soil bacteria are counted under a microscope
seeds are treated with radiation before sowing
explanation: Explants are grown aseptically on a nutrient medium containing hormones, producing many genetically identical plants from one parent.

text: The Human Genome Project was undertaken to
options: determine the complete sequence of human DNA
eliminate all inherited diseases by surgery
map the human nervous system in three dimensions
explanation: The project, declared complete in 2003, identified the sequence of the roughly three billion base pairs in human DNA.

text: Crops carrying a gene transferred from another species are commonly known as
explanation: Transgenic or genetically modified crops such as Bt cotton contain a gene introduced from an unrelated organism by recombinant DNA methods.

text: Which storage device stores data using no moving mechanical parts?
explanation: A solid state drive records data in flash memory chips, so it has no spinning platters or read-write heads.

text: The process of starting a computer and loading the operating system into memory is called
explanation: Booting is the start-up sequence in which firmware tests the hardware and then loads the operating system from storage into RAM.

text: Remote sensing satellites are used chiefly to
options: collect information about the Earth's surface from orbit
measure cosmic rays beyond the solar system
explanation: Remote sensing satellites carry cameras and sensors that record land use, crops, forests and other surface features from orbit.

text: The device that supplies power to a computer for a short time during a mains failure is a
explanation: A UPS holds a battery that takes over instantly when mains power fails, giving time to save work and shut down safely.
